prior_decision_text.runs/pr-evaluation-audit-001/h200/RANKIN:
# H200 experiment order

Assessed 2026-10-20 against the running eight-H200 node. These are **untested
H200 hypotheses**. Rank means expected learning/useful improvement per unit of
integration and GPU time. It does not mean largest possible eventual speedup.
Numerical ranges below are engineering planning scenarios, not measurements or
confidence intervals; zero and regressions remain possible.

## Actual scope

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`.
- Two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas; API2 each; eight H200s total.
- vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev493+gac9126e58`, image `sha256:3d17635c5aa0340e2f2502c067ce4b587d8e7dc678195e90b71142490dc6d71c`.
- Installed serving checkout `11c249d28b2962f7384b4ab1fd7c1664704e7524`, branch
  `more_metrics`. This is newer than the audit's serving snapshot.
- **64 sequences per DP engine**, not the audit's 128-sequence R7b override.
  MBT16384, context1048576, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, prefix cache enabled,
  real DSpark k5/block rejection/adaptive OFF. Verbose request/output/delta
  logging and graph/speculation metrics are enabled. Keep these identical in A/B.
- H200 is SM90; the audit's MegaAttention/MegaMoE/SM100 assumptions do not carry
  over. `nvidia-smi` reports 143771 MiB per GPU and driver580.126.20.

## Ranked Queue

| Rank | Candidate | H200 validity and cheapest falsification | Potential end-to-end delta and effort |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Share FlashMLA plans, PR58818**; reopened B200 exclusion | Installed MRV2/SWA code creates per-group holders, and the three-file patch applies cleanly. Same SM90 mechanism has H20 evidence. Verify redundant planner launches on this TP1/DP4 path; TP8's exact counts are not guaranteed. | Planning range: **0-3% lower low-load decode TPOT**, often **0-1% at saturation**. Three Python files, no dependency rebuild. Best first cheap test, modest ceiling. |
| 2 | **E02: logical drafter rows, PR58984** | Installed `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync` uses target graph capacity (`target_dp_sync.num_reqs`). With adaptive OFF, count real requests versus padded drafter rows under ragged arrivals. Stop if equal. | **0-10%** is a broad test scenario only where padding wastes material work; likely near zero at aligned full batches. Four-file patch, DP correctness tests and an older-base port review. |
| 3 | **E04: CPU DP collectives, PR61767** | New `cpu_all_reduce_` is absent in inspected installed files. Both replicas synchronize four DP ranks. Measure exposed CPU collective time, excluding rank-arrival skew. | **0-5%** scenario if dispatch gaps dominate; zero if hidden by GPU work. More distributed correctness risk than #1. No kernel/toolchain rebuild expected. |
| 4 | **E07: draft token-budget accounting, PR59468** | Check reservations and budget-limited prefill admission at existing MBT16384. Real bound here is **64*(5-1)=256 tokens/rank**, only **1.5625%** of the budget. | Usually near-zero decode gain; potentially small burst TTFT improvement. Budget fraction is **not** a speedup bound or prediction. A lower-MBT experiment would be a different arm. |
| 5 | **E10: host Engram allocation/placement** | Offload and DP sharing/sharding exist, but resolve the actual branch before choosing #59849, #59923 or #62359. Verify NUMA locality and allocator capabilities. | No defensible numeric serving estimate yet. Most plausible in prefill/host-memory stalls. Registration/NUMA branches differ; GB200 cuMem results are not H200 guarantees. |
| 6 | **E11/E14: prefix-group and final-rank locality** | Measure actual prefix misses per rank on agent-f75/sessions. API2 matters; endpoint affinity is already different from DP-rank affinity. | Could improve TTFT substantially on demonstrated misses; **zero expected benefit on the selected cache-isolated first diagnostic**. Do not adopt older-V4 patches unchanged. |
| 7 | **E12/E13: scheduler work and prefill alignment** | Measure host scheduling spans and rank skew under mixed prefill/decode. Revalidate source membership per patch. | Profile-dependent; no justified percentage yet. More likely to affect tails than short homogeneous decode. |
| 8 | **SM90 candidate-only indexer scoring, issue61830** | Real Hopper gap: candidate consumers compute dense logits then mask them. Existing SM100 sparse-MQA route cannot be enabled on H200. Needs an actual Hopper implementation. | Larger long-context ceiling, but poor first-test time-to-value. H20 report puts four consumer layers at **20% of a 1M-context step** at one tested load: even perfect removal implies at most **25% throughput** there before other effects. This says nothing comparable about 1K/8K traffic. |
| 9 | **E15/E18: fusion or alternate Hopper MoE/communication backend** | TP1 may expose useful fusion/communication changes; kernel and precision eligibility must be established first. Current MoE all-to-all config is `allgather_reducescatter`. | Potentially larger gains but integration, numerical and memory risk. Separate backend/precision/topology arms; no percentage justified from the current audit. |

Primary evidence: [#58818](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58818),
[#58984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58984),
[#61767](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61767),
[#59468](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59468),
[SM90 indexer request #61830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61830).
The remaining source links and restrictions are in the original experiment cards.

## Important Rejections

| Audit direction | H200 disposition |
|---|---|
| E01 / #61039 length-aware candidate selection | **Do not cherry-pick as a ready H200 win.** `has_deep_select()` in installed `sparse_mqa_logits.py:43` requires SM100. Upstream's length-aware route uses it; the fallback keeps full-width scoring/top-k. A Hopper port is separate work. |
| E06 / #60802 DeepSelect dispatch | Installed `IndexerTopKDispatcher` also gates DeepSelect to SM100. The proposed route is unavailable on this H200 build. |
| E03 / graph cap512 ->768/1024 and #62040 | **No immediate experiment at seq64.** Live startup captured target FULL(384 tokens,64 requests,q6) and draft FULL(320,64,q5). The specific largest-batch hole is absent. Reopen on runtime fallback or a later seq128 arm, not by copying B200 settings. |
| E05 MegaMoE JIT warmup | Separate startup objective; Blackwell MegaMoE patch is not a steady-state Hopper improvement. Existing startup was already in progress. |
| E08 packed MX activation chain, E09 B200 FlashMLA#227, SM100 routes in E18 | Not eligible as direct Hopper changes. These need architecture-specific ports or a different backend hypothesis. |
| E16 KV tier, E17 draft-context/adaptive changes | Offload tier is inactive; short-context pilot does not trigger long-draft degradation. Added features/output changes have lower first-experiment ROI. |

The source-level H200 exclusions are supported by the installed code and
[#61039's implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7c3f7e5500c85aacb72aab50bd1ce05485b1d73a/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py).
The graph-hole mechanism is documented in
[#62040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62040).

## Why #58818 First

The upstream H20 author reports +2.5% output TPS at C1 and +0.5% at C64, with
synthetic acceptance in the performance runs. We will use real rejection and
the actual H200 TP1/DP4 topology. Those differences limit transferability. The
upstream correctness runs used real verification, but their unit tests did
**not** exercise the newly shared-cache branch. Our candidate is unqualified
until that branch and actual decode behavior are checked.

For intuition, if duplicate plans cost 0.3 ms on a 15 ms critical-path step,
removing them saves 2% step latency and raises ideal throughput by about 2.04%.
The H200 planner count/time and exposed fraction must be measured. Neither
GPU bandwidth ratios nor the PR's microbenchmark multiplier predicts serving
throughput.

Keep a measured no-win outcome: a 0.5% effect below boot/run variation is a
reason to move to #58984, not to keep running until a favorable sample appears.

target.gpu: 8x NVIDIA H200 SM90, 143771 MiB per GPU
target.topology: two independent four-GPU TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas, API2 each
target.workload: Preserve native agent-f75 8K/1K prefix workload and fixed-schedule Mooncake anchors, adapted explicitly to H200 seq64; separate 1K/1K cache-isolated diagnostic and long-context, ragged, mixed, cold/warm held-out diagnostics.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compare dense, gather and direct paged scoring on identical captured inputs across observed row counts and compressed lengths, including one request and the native 8K/1K workload. Include every preparation, scoring, top-k and remap stage.
alternatives.explanation: Dense scoring wins on H200 because short contexts, few rows or TP1 indexer shapes make candidate bookkeeping more expensive than discarded scoring.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Measure server-token-based request TPOT and whole-run completion goodput; record exact tokens, rank-local prefix hits and all-rank acceptance counters. Use matched-shape diagnostics separately to attribute kernel work.
alternatives.explanation: Lower client ITL reflects acceptance, streaming chunks, prefix-cache state or batch composition rather than a faster serving path.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Keep the selector backend fixed across arms and time preparation, scoring, selection and remapping separately at identical shapes. Compare gather and direct scoring using the same candidate set and compact width.
alternatives.explanation: Any benefit comes mainly from top-k operating on fewer logits, rather than direct scoring or avoided K copies.

card.applicability: Deferred long-context candidate. Target H200 is SM90, but FP8 attention KV settings alone do not prove indexer-cache eligibility. Confirm actual indexer heads, strides, candidate widths, causal metadata and architecture gates. TP1's 64 attention heads neither prove nor disprove indexer-kernel compatibility. Candidate-source layers, pre-candidate layers and prefill remain outside the proposed change. Model accuracy, short-workload safety and H200 effect size are unknown.
card.code_surface: vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_paged_logits.py; sparse_attn_indexer.py; vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py; vllm/envs.py; tests/kernels/attention/test_candidate_paged_logits.py. Alternative arm: candidate_gather.py and its supplied integration paths. The supplied patch excerpts do not include complete scoring and dispatch bodies.

evidence.quote: This is one A/B pair, not a confidence-interval result.
Accuracy and shorter-workload checks are still pending.

experiment.control: Pinned baseline dense scoring plus candidate masking and the unchanged deployed top-k backend. Use three mutually exclusive static arms: dense with both candidate flags off; #62000 gather only; #62463 direct paged only. Dense is the strongest simple short-context comparator. Calibrate and freeze any gather workload gates before held-out evaluation; FORCE is for validation, not a production policy.
experiment.correctness: Validate scores against an independent FP32 reference with justified tolerances, tie-aware selection against dense scoring, and a model-quality subset. Exercise invalid, duplicate and padded candidate handling; empty/partial contexts; request-local remapping; block64 layouts and strides; speculative causal bounds; and unchanged source-layer behavior. Capture short contexts and replay with changed lengths, pages and request assignments; compare eager results and check stable workspace allocation. Author-described tests are not evidence they passed on H200. Map to applicable G01-G05 when definitions are available.
experiment.cost: Higher integration and verification cost than plan sharing: complete kernel/dispatch review, numerical validation and three-arm comparison are required. Gate expensive long-context tests on eligibility and the unprofiled screen. Measure workspace and KV-capacity effects rather than infer them. Report P*T/(3600*N_output), with unknown full-node hourly price P; also report qualified-token cost. Profiled runs are excluded from the serving frontier.
experiment.held_out_condition: Previously unseen long-context lengths, single-request decode, ragged mixtures spanning short and long contexts, cold/warm prefixes, page-table remapping, preemption and mixed prefill/decode. Determine feasible H200 concurrency from actual KV residency; do not import H20 capacity.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Only profiler-derived timings or streamed ITL improve; acceptance or prefix behavior cannot be joined to requests; eligible opportunity coverage is inadequate; the GPU correctness report is missing; or independent full-run intervals cannot distinguish benefit from regression.
experiment.metrics: Activation: candidate-path consumer calls and rows divided by all structurally eligible consumer calls and rows, stratified by live compressed length, row count, eager/graph mode and rank. Record fallback reasons and whether consumer mask kernels disappear. Measure request TPOT using exact server output tokens, TTFT tails, throughput, historical-scorer goodput, replay lag, all-rank draft/verify/accepted deltas, prefix hits, KV blocks, preemption and workspace high-water marks. Separate diagnostics measure the complete indexer path, not mismatched scoring buckets.
experiment.rejects_if: The feature already executes equivalently; required cache or shape contracts cannot be satisfied; numerical, causal or replay correctness fails without a credible repair; or adequately powered tests show no useful improvement over dense or the strongest eligible alternative. A native-workload regression rejects blanket activation even if a long-context diagnostic improves.
experiment.supports_if: All relevant ranks exercise the intended path; reference, graph and model-quality checks pass; complete-path time falls at matched inputs; and unprofiled paired intervals demonstrate useful TPOT or goodput improvement without unacceptable primary-workload or tail regressions. A long-context-only win supports only that scope, not deployment-wide promotion.
experiment.treatment: Start with source/configuration membership and eligibility checks. After activation and correctness, screen each arm unprofiled on native agent-f75 and fixed-schedule Mooncake at seq64, then run separate long-context and cache-isolated diagnostics. Compare surviving arms in at least five alternating paired full-run blocks for small gains. Keep topology, speculation, prefixes, logging and scheduler settings fixed. Do not add a host context-length branch inside captured execution; any future mixed-workload routing requires separate graph-safe qualification.

card.mechanism: Implementation evidence: #62463 exposes direct paged candidate scoring with compact logits and device-side causal-bound preparation; #62000 exposes candidate-K gathering and default-off controls. Both avoid full compressed-context scoring for consumers. Transfer inference: direct reads may additionally avoid gather workspace traffic and fixed copy cost. Benefits depend on actual indexer shapes and context-to-candidate width, not TP-local attention-head padding.

novelty.implementation: Adapt an explicit SM90 implementation to the pinned TP1 deployment and validate graph-live inputs.
novelty.nearest_prior_art: vLLM #62463 direct paged scoring and #62000 gather-based scoring, both addressing #61830.
novelty.scientific: Existing candidate-restricted scoring; no new algorithm claimed.
novelty.specific_delta: Replace consumer dense-score-then-mask execution with direct candidate scoring, conditional on eligibility; retain dense execution where the alternative lacks serving value.
novelty.workload: Resolve conflicting low-concurrency evidence and test whether long-context benefits survive native prefix traffic and H200 seq64 execution.

card.observed_bottleneck: No H200 scoring bottleneck is measured. #62000 reports profiler-derived improvements at approximately 1M context and nine requests on H20 TP8, but an approximately 11.6% single-request regression. #62463 reports lower mean ITL on H20 TP8 with 1,029,974 input and 16,384 output tokens, using only one run per arm and 2/4/8/16 requests at C1/2/4/8. At C4, overall completion throughput fell 1.5%. Its profiling batches also differed. These are author-reported results, not independently verified H200 observations.
card.predicted_direction: Potentially lower consumer-indexer time and long-context TPOT, especially when dense scoring scans substantially more positions than the candidate set. Short-context or low-row regressions remain plausible. No capacity, general throughput or primary-workload improvement is established.
card.proposed_change: First inspect complete installed call sites, patch integration, FP8 indexer-cache layout, context-parallel configuration and actual consumer dispatch. If eligible and absent, adapt #62463 to the pinned branch while preserving live device inputs and configuration-based graph selection. Keep dense scoring available. Evaluate #62000 as a separate mutually exclusive comparator; do not stack the implementations or infer a profitable H200 threshold from its example settings.
card.revision_reason: Initial proposal incorporates the gather single-request regression and direct-scoring sample limitations by comparing alternatives within one hypothesis, retaining dense control and restricting any claim to demonstrated workloads.
card.statement: Test direct paged candidate-only indexer scoring as a conditional replacement for dense scoring followed by masking in consumer layers. The supplied #62463 patch describes reading candidate K in place and retaining device-resident live lengths; #62000 instead gathers K before scoring. These are competing implementations of the same work-elimination mechanism, not cumulative optimizations. H20 evidence is conflicting: gathering regressed at one request, while direct scoring's lower ITL came from tiny samples and did not consistently improve throughput. The transfer hypothesis is that avoiding both discarded scoring and intermediate K copies helps eligible H200 long-context decode. First establish actual indexer shapes, cache format and baseline dispatch. Keep dense scoring as the short-context comparator and default; require native 8K/1K evidence before claiming a useful change to this deployment.

policy.baseline_comparison: Use the supplied live attestation: vLLM ac9126e58aa7bbab1856ba6593ba4d5003fea516, serving checkout 11c249d28b2962f7384b4ab1fd7c1664704e7524, and the supplied image/model revision. Hardware is eight H200 SM90 GPUs, 143771 MiB each, arranged as two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas with API2 each. Preserve seq64, MBT16384, context1048576, graphcap512, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, embedding_across_dp, prefix caching, DSpark k5 probabilistic draft/block rejection, adaptive OFF, no-swa-bounded-replay and enabled telemetry except where explicitly varied. Primary comparisons preserve native agent-f75 8K/1K prefixes and fixed-schedule Mooncake anchors adapted to H200 seq64. Keep cache-isolated 1K/1K and long-context, ragged, mixed, cold/warm diagnostics separate. Seq128 is a separate arm. Verify attention/MoE dispatch and the reported allgather_reducescatter configuration; endpoint availability does not establish kernel activation.

criteria.description: REQUIRED VETO: Identify a credible, testable mechanism connecting the proposed change to task value, plus either a concrete baseline delta or an explicit cheap source/configuration/log inspection that determines whether the feature is already present and active. State the strongest simple comparator, including an existing flag or parameter adjustment where applicable. A demonstrated absence of both a useful delta and a credible improvement mechanism fails this gate. Unresolved baseline membership or bottleneck exposure defers judgment and motivates inspection; measured speedup is not required.
criteria.justification: The supplied baseline says, "No measured bottleneck or new GPU result." Several proposed directions may already exist or only matter under specific traffic. This receives the largest weight because useful incremental value, rather than publication status, is the selection objective.

criteria.description: REQUIRED VETO: Provide a plausible implementation, activation or explicit port path for SM90 and the pinned serving branches, with scoped correctness checks. Address relevant G01-G05 checks, numerical changes, graph/cache branches and distributed behavior; use a quality subset when math changes. Speculative acceptance is a diagnostic, not a correctness score. Demonstrated incompatibility or correctness failure without a credible remedy fails this gate. Unknown dispatch, branch membership or correctness remains deferred. An explicit Hopper port is eligible even when a direct SM100 activation is unavailable.
criteria.justification: The research must reopen B200 exclusions without assuming that Blackwell kernels, topology, precision paths or graph settings transfer to H200. Applicability and correctness are necessary gates, while implementation effort is assessed separately.

criteria.description: Specify the activation signal and eligible-opportunity denominator, competing explanations, strongest simple comparator, scoped correctness checks, held-out test and prospective support/reject/inconclusive rules. Follow attestation, activation, correctness, unprofiled screening, separate mechanism diagnosis, then paired confirmation and held-out evaluation. Use all-replica/rank coverage, request TPOT=(last-first token time)/(server output tokens-1), TTFT tails and relevant draft, KV, preemption, goodput or replay counters. Confirm small gains with at least five alternating paired full-run blocks, drift checks and intervals; avoid request-level pseudoreplication. Missing telemetry or inadequately covered zero hits is inconclusive. Exclude profiled measurements from the serving frontier.
criteria.justification: The evaluator contract is unusually specific, and likely effects may depend on padding, rank skew, prefix reuse or load. A discriminating experiment deserves substantial weight because it can expose a useful mechanism or cheaply falsify one without an existing bottleneck measurement.

criteria.description: Separate observed results, source-author claims, source fixes and transfer inference. Use short exact quotations and inspect the implementation or engineering artifact supporting the proposed mechanism. Record source hardware, workload, effect size and limitations as unknown whenever absent. Investigate negative results and branch/deployment restrictions. A paper abstract does not establish implementation behavior; prior ranking prose does not establish current source membership.
criteria.justification: No direct evidence accompanies this request. Traceability matters, but demanding multiple publications would unnecessarily exclude straightforward flag changes and small implementation fixes. One relevant engineering source can be sufficient.

criteria.description: Prefer inexpensive falsification, manageable integration and rollback, and benefits exposed by the primary workload. Identify when value is confined to a diagnostic regime. Consider memory pressure, quality, tail latency and throughput tradeoffs. Use parameterized eight-GPU node cost until H200 pricing is known. Across the five selections, favor complementary mechanisms and workload coverage to reduce redundant experiments, without requiring unpublished techniques.
criteria.justification: The requested output is a diverse, practical experiment shortlist. A cheap planner or scheduling change and a larger communication or long-context port can both merit consideration, but their integration costs, activation opportunities and learning value differ.

evidence.rationale: Require one directly relevant engineering source per supported selection, such as implementation code, a patch, a reproducible issue or a dispatch trace; multiple independent sources and papers are not universal requirements. Missing evidence defers qualification rather than proving the idea ineffective. Inspect relevant full-text methods/results if relying on a paper beyond its abstract. Observed results: no independent measurements or implementation artifacts are supplied; available_evidence is empty, and the runtime details are user-supplied attestation. Author claims: the prior ranking says "the three-file patch applies cleanly" and describes H20 performance runs as using "synthetic acceptance"; neither is verified here. Transfer inference: these statements motivate source and activation checks, not H200 gain predictions. The target hardware and workload are specified; candidate-specific hardware, workload, effect sizes and limitations remain unknown except where explicitly attributed to unverified ranking statements. Current dispatch, measured bottlenecks, H200 effects, node price and production SLO remain unknown.

policy.objective: Select five practical hypotheses for useful improvements over the supplied DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash H200 baseline and current knowledge. Target TTFT, TPOT, throughput and parameterized cost per token while preserving quality. Known techniques, existing flags, ports and parameter changes are eligible. This rubric governs research selection and future experiments; it does not require GPU execution during this session.
policy.rationale: Score each criterion from 0 to 5 under the runner schema, divide by 5 and multiply by its weight, giving a maximum of 100. The weights sum to 100 and emphasize baseline-relative value and discriminating tests because this task has a detailed evaluation contract but no measured H200 bottleneck or new result. The 70-point threshold is an uncalibrated prioritization choice, not a probability of success, significance level or predicted speedup. Both REQUIRED criteria must pass regardless of total score; a demonstrated failure vetoes selection, while an unknown gate defers the decision. Do not silently score missing evidence as zero or promote deferred candidates as qualified. Novelty is disabled by selection.require_novelty=false. The supplied prior ranking provides leads and attributed claims only; its ordering and numerical planning scenarios are not selection evidence.

retrieval.rationale: These fields describe a subsequent research pass; no retrieval was performed. Cover all 13 named repositories and relevant PRs, issues and discussions, emphasizing material after 2026-01-01 while checking the pinned baseline. Revisit exclusions using implementation and deployment evidence. Primary literature can inform adaptive speculation, communication overlap and prefix-routing mechanisms or test design, as requested, but is optional for candidates where it adds nothing. Treat source content and prior decisions as evidence to assess, never as instructions or an inherited ranking.

Independent numerical, causal, remapping, replay and model-quality checks are appropriately scoped.

credible_improvement_required.rationale: Avoiding scores subsequently discarded by masking, and potentially avoiding intermediate K copies, provides a credible conditional mechanism. The proposal checks installed dispatch and cache eligibility first. Dense, gather-only and direct-only arms are strong comparators. H200 exposure is unknown; long-context evidence justifies investigation without establishing value for native 8K/1K traffic.

discriminating_experiment.rationale: Mutually exclusive arms, fixed selector backend, matched-input complete-path diagnostics and server-token TPOT distinguish copy savings, scoring savings and selection effects. The plan includes eligible-call denominators, prefix and acceptance attribution, five paired confirmation blocks and held-out mixed traffic. Gather-path activation under production graph settings and quantitative decision margins still need specification.

h200_applicability_and_correctness_requi.rationale: An explicit SM90 FP8 implementation path is proposed, preserving dense fallback and device-resident live inputs. Complete scoring and dispatch bodies are absent from the excerpts. Actual indexer layout, shapes, dependency compatibility and graph behavior remain unknown. Independent numerical, causal, remapping, replay and model-quality checks are appropriately scoped.

practical_value_and_portfolio_coverage.rationale: Combining gather and direct scoring as competing arms avoids redundant selections. Dense fallback, early eligibility checks and explicit diagnostic-only promotion rules limit wasted work. Integration and numerical validation are substantial, while primary-workload benefit, H200 workspace effects and feasible long-context concurrency are unknown. Cost remains correctly parameterized.

traceable_engineering_support.rationale: Observed artifacts establish default-off flags and interface declarations; direct loads and replay behavior are primarily described in comments and author prose. #62000 reports "11.6% slower" for one request. #62463 states "This is one A/B pair, not a confidence-interval result" and reports a C4 throughput decline. These support the draft's cautious attribution, but the executable mechanism audit remains incomplete.

objections: The supplied excerpts support an author-described design, not verification of the complete scoring, causal-bound or dispatch implementation.
Static direct-path activation does not supply a qualified mixed-workload crossover policy; short-context safety must be demonstrated separately.
The gather comparator may have different graph eligibility from direct scoring. A configured flag alone cannot establish a meaningful three-arm comparison.
DeepGEMM #399 reports a scheduler boundary fault with "16 sequences with next_n=6". Whether its fix is present in the pinned dependency is unknown and relevant to the dense reference.
review.required_revision: Retain as a deferred long-context candidate. Separate inspected flag/interface code from author-described kernel behavior. Require complete scoring and dispatch review, reconcile the MQA API changes described in #61149, and check #399 fix membership. Define graph eligibility for each arm without using FORCE as production policy. Freeze numerical tolerances, quality and latency margins, run budgets and long-context-only promotion rules. Weighted score: 72/100; the unknown applicability gate prevents qualification.

plan.execution_requires: Fresh attestation and unresolved activation/correctness/build prerequisites; model deferral is not overridden.

experiment.control: Pinned baseline dense scoring plus candidate masking and the unchanged deployed top-k backend. Use three mutually exclusive static arms: dense with both candidate flags off; #62000 gather only; #62463 direct paged only. Dense is the strongest simple short-context comparator. Calibrate and freeze any gather workload gates before held-out evaluation; FORCE is for validation, not a production policy.
experiment.correctness: Validate scores against an independent FP32 reference with justified tolerances, tie-aware selection against dense scoring, and a model-quality subset. Exercise invalid, duplicate and padded candidate handling; empty/partial contexts; request-local remapping; block64 layouts and strides; speculative causal bounds; and unchanged source-layer behavior. Capture short contexts and replay with changed lengths, pages and request assignments; compare eager results and check stable workspace allocation. Author-described tests are not evidence they passed on H200. Map to applicable G01-G05 when definitions are available.
experiment.cost: Higher integration and verification cost than plan sharing: complete kernel/dispatch review, numerical validation and three-arm comparison are required. Gate expensive long-context tests on eligibility and the unprofiled screen. Measure workspace and KV-capacity effects rather than infer them. Report P*T/(3600*N_output), with unknown full-node hourly price P; also report qualified-token cost. Profiled runs are excluded from the serving frontier.
experiment.held_out_condition: Previously unseen long-context lengths, single-request decode, ragged mixtures spanning short and long contexts, cold/warm prefixes, page-table remapping, preemption and mixed prefill/decode. Determine feasible H200 concurrency from actual KV residency; do not import H20 capacity.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Only profiler-derived timings or streamed ITL improve; acceptance or prefix behavior cannot be joined to requests; eligible opportunity coverage is inadequate; the GPU correctness report is missing; or independent full-run intervals cannot distinguish benefit from regression.
experiment.metrics: Activation: candidate-path consumer calls and rows divided by all structurally eligible consumer calls and rows, stratified by live compressed length, row count, eager/graph mode and rank. Record fallback reasons and whether consumer mask kernels disappear. Measure request TPOT using exact server output tokens, TTFT tails, throughput, historical-scorer goodput, replay lag, all-rank draft/verify/accepted deltas, prefix hits, KV blocks, preemption and workspace high-water marks. Separate diagnostics measure the complete indexer path, not mismatched scoring buckets.
experiment.rejects_if: The feature already executes equivalently; required cache or shape contracts cannot be satisfied; numerical, causal or replay correctness fails without a credible repair; or adequately powered tests show no useful improvement over dense or the strongest eligible alternative. A native-workload regression rejects blanket activation even if a long-context diagnostic improves.
experiment.supports_if: All relevant ranks exercise the intended path; reference, graph and model-quality checks pass; complete-path time falls at matched inputs; and unprofiled paired intervals demonstrate useful TPOT or goodput improvement without unacceptable primary-workload or tail regressions. A long-context-only win supports only that scope, not deployment-wide promotion.
experiment.treatment: Start with source/configuration membership and eligibility checks. After activation and correctness, screen each arm unprofiled on native agent-f75 and fixed-schedule Mooncake at seq64, then run separate long-context and cache-isolated diagnostics. Compare surviving arms in at least five alternating paired full-run blocks for small gains. Keep topology, speculation, prefixes, logging and scheduler settings fixed. Do not add a host context-length branch inside captured execution; any future mixed-workload routing requires separate graph-safe qualification.

prior_decision_text.runs/pr-evaluation-audit-001/h200/RANKIN:
# H200 experiment order

Assessed 2026-10-20 against the running eight-H200 node. These are **untested
H200 hypotheses**. Rank means expected learning/useful improvement per unit of
integration and GPU time. It does not mean largest possible eventual speedup.
Numerical ranges below are engineering planning scenarios, not measurements or
confidence intervals; zero and regressions remain possible.

## Actual scope

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`.
- Two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas; API2 each; eight H200s total.
- vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev493+gac9126e58`, image `sha256:3d17635c5aa0340e2f2502c067ce4b587d8e7dc678195e90b71142490dc6d71c`.
- Installed serving checkout `11c249d28b2962f7384b4ab1fd7c1664704e7524`, branch
  `more_metrics`. This is newer than the audit's serving snapshot.
- **64 sequences per DP engine**, not the audit's 128-sequence R7b override.
  MBT16384, context1048576, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, prefix cache enabled,
  real DSpark k5/block rejection/adaptive OFF. Verbose request/output/delta
  logging and graph/speculation metrics are enabled. Keep these identical in A/B.
- H200 is SM90; the audit's MegaAttention/MegaMoE/SM100 assumptions do not carry
  over. `nvidia-smi` reports 143771 MiB per GPU and driver580.126.20.

## Ranked Queue

| Rank | Candidate | H200 validity and cheapest falsification | Potential end-to-end delta and effort |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Share FlashMLA plans, PR58818**; reopened B200 exclusion | Installed MRV2/SWA code creates per-group holders, and the three-file patch applies cleanly. Same SM90 mechanism has H20 evidence. Verify redundant planner launches on this TP1/DP4 path; TP8's exact counts are not guaranteed. | Planning range: **0-3% lower low-load decode TPOT**, often **0-1% at saturation**. Three Python files, no dependency rebuild. Best first cheap test, modest ceiling. |
| 2 | **E02: logical drafter rows, PR58984** | Installed `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync` uses target graph capacity (`target_dp_sync.num_reqs`). With adaptive OFF, count real requests versus padded drafter rows under ragged arrivals. Stop if equal. | **0-10%** is a broad test scenario only where padding wastes material work; likely near zero at aligned full batches. Four-file patch, DP correctness tests and an older-base port review. |
| 3 | **E04: CPU DP collectives, PR61767** | New `cpu_all_reduce_` is absent in inspected installed files. Both replicas synchronize four DP ranks. Measure exposed CPU collective time, excluding rank-arrival skew. | **0-5%** scenario if dispatch gaps dominate; zero if hidden by GPU work. More distributed correctness risk than #1. No kernel/toolchain rebuild expected. |
| 4 | **E07: draft token-budget accounting, PR59468** | Check reservations and budget-limited prefill admission at existing MBT16384. Real bound here is **64*(5-1)=256 tokens/rank**, only **1.5625%** of the budget. | Usually near-zero decode gain; potentially small burst TTFT improvement. Budget fraction is **not** a speedup bound or prediction. A lower-MBT experiment would be a different arm. |
| 5 | **E10: host Engram allocation/placement** | Offload and DP sharing/sharding exist, but resolve the actual branch before choosing #59849, #59923 or #62359. Verify NUMA locality and allocator capabilities. | No defensible numeric serving estimate yet. Most plausible in prefill/host-memory stalls. Registration/NUMA branches differ; GB200 cuMem results are not H200 guarantees. |
| 6 | **E11/E14: prefix-group and final-rank locality** | Measure actual prefix misses per rank on agent-f75/sessions. API2 matters; endpoint affinity is already different from DP-rank affinity. | Could improve TTFT substantially on demonstrated misses; **zero expected benefit on the selected cache-isolated first diagnostic**. Do not adopt older-V4 patches unchanged. |
| 7 | **E12/E13: scheduler work and prefill alignment** | Measure host scheduling spans and rank skew under mixed prefill/decode. Revalidate source membership per patch. | Profile-dependent; no justified percentage yet. More likely to affect tails than short homogeneous decode. |
| 8 | **SM90 candidate-only indexer scoring, issue61830** | Real Hopper gap: candidate consumers compute dense logits then mask them. Existing SM100 sparse-MQA route cannot be enabled on H200. Needs an actual Hopper implementation. | Larger long-context ceiling, but poor first-test time-to-value. H20 report puts four consumer layers at **20% of a 1M-context step** at one tested load: even perfect removal implies at most **25% throughput** there before other effects. This says nothing comparable about 1K/8K traffic. |
| 9 | **E15/E18: fusion or alternate Hopper MoE/communication backend** | TP1 may expose useful fusion/communication changes; kernel and precision eligibility must be established first. Current MoE all-to-all config is `allgather_reducescatter`. | Potentially larger gains but integration, numerical and memory risk. The remaining source links and restrictions are in the original experiment cards.

## Important Rejections

| Audit direction | H200 disposition |
|---|---|
| E01 / #61039 length-aware candidate selection | **Do not cherry-pick as a ready H200 win.** `has_deep_select()` in installed `sparse_mqa_logits.py:43` requires SM100. Upstream's length-aware route uses it; the fallback keeps full-width scoring/top-k. A Hopper port is separate work. |
| E06 / #60802 DeepSelect dispatch | Installed `IndexerTopKDispatcher` also gates DeepSelect to SM100. The proposed route is unavailable on this H200 build. |
| E03 / graph cap512 ->768/1024 and #62040 | **No immediate experiment at seq64.** Live startup captured target FULL(384 tokens,64 requests,q6) and draft FULL(320,64,q5). The specific largest-batch hole is absent. Reopen on runtime fallback or a later seq128 arm, not by copying B200 settings. |
| E05 MegaMoE JIT warmup | Separate startup objective; Blackwell MegaMoE patch is not a steady-state Hopper improvement. Existing startup was already in progress. |
| E08 packed MX activation chain, E09 B200 FlashMLA#227, SM100 routes in E18 | Not eligible as direct Hopper changes. These need architecture-specific ports or a different backend hypothesis. |
| E16 KV tier, E17 draft-context/adaptive changes | Offload tier is inactive; short-context pilot does not trigger long-draft degradation. Added features/output changes have lower first-experiment ROI. |

The source-level H200 exclusions are supported by the installed code and
[#61039's implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7c3f7e5500c85aacb72aab50bd1ce05485b1d73a/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py).
The graph-hole mechanism is documented in
[#62040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62040).

## Why #58818 First

The upstream H20 author reports +2.5% output TPS at C1 and +0.5% at C64, with
synthetic acceptance in the performance runs. We will use real rejection and
the actual H200 TP1/DP4 topology. Those differences limit transferability. The
upstream correctness runs used real verification, but their unit tests did
**not** exercise the newly shared-cache branch. Our candidate is unqualified
until that branch and actual decode behavior are checked.

For intuition, if duplicate plans cost 0.3 ms on a 15 ms critical-path step,
removing them saves 2% step latency and raises ideal throughput by about 2.04%.
The H200 planner count/time and exposed fraction must be measured. Neither
GPU bandwidth ratios nor the PR's microbenchmark multiplier predicts serving
throughput.

Keep a measured no-win outcome: a 0.5% effect below boot/run variation is a
reason to move to #58984, not to keep running until a favorable sample appears.

prior_decision_text.runs/pr-evaluation-audit-001/h200/RANKIN:
# H200 experiment order

Assessed 2026-10-20 against the running eight-H200 node. These are **untested
H200 hypotheses**. Rank means expected learning/useful improvement per unit of
integration and GPU time. It does not mean largest possible eventual speedup.
Numerical ranges below are engineering planning scenarios, not measurements or
confidence intervals; zero and regressions remain possible.

## Actual scope

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`.
- Two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas; API2 each; eight H200s total.
- vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev493+gac9126e58`, image `sha256:3d17635c5aa0340e2f2502c067ce4b587d8e7dc678195e90b71142490dc6d71c`.
- Installed serving checkout `11c249d28b2962f7384b4ab1fd7c1664704e7524`, branch
  `more_metrics`. This is newer than the audit's serving snapshot.
- **64 sequences per DP engine**, not the audit's 128-sequence R7b override.
  MBT16384, context1048576, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, prefix cache enabled,
  real DSpark k5/block rejection/adaptive OFF. Verbose request/output/delta
  logging and graph/speculation metrics are enabled. Keep these identical in A/B.
- H200 is SM90; the audit's MegaAttention/MegaMoE/SM100 assumptions do not carry
  over. `nvidia-smi` reports 143771 MiB per GPU and driver580.126.20.

## Ranked Queue

| Rank | Candidate | H200 validity and cheapest falsification | Potential end-to-end delta and effort |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Share FlashMLA plans, PR58818**; reopened B200 exclusion | Installed MRV2/SWA code creates per-group holders, and the three-file patch applies cleanly. Same SM90 mechanism has H20 evidence. Verify redundant planner launches on this TP1/DP4 path; TP8's exact counts are not guaranteed. | Planning range: **0-3% lower low-load decode TPOT**, often **0-1% at saturation**. Three Python files, no dependency rebuild. Best first cheap test, modest ceiling. |
| 2 | **E02: logical drafter rows, PR58984** | Installed `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync` uses target graph capacity (`target_dp_sync.num_reqs`). With adaptive OFF, count real requests versus padded drafter rows under ragged arrivals. Stop if equal. | **0-10%** is a broad test scenario only where padding wastes material work; likely near zero at aligned full batches. Four-file patch, DP correctness tests and an older-base port review. |
| 3 | **E04: CPU DP collectives, PR61767** | New `cpu_all_reduce_` is absent in inspected installed files. Both replicas synchronize four DP ranks. Measure exposed CPU collective time, excluding rank-arrival skew. | **0-5%** scenario if dispatch gaps dominate; zero if hidden by GPU work. More distributed correctness risk than #1. No kernel/toolchain rebuild expected. |
| 4 | **E07: draft token-budget accounting, PR59468** | Check reservations and budget-limited prefill admission at existing MBT16384. Real bound here is **64*(5-1)=256 tokens/rank**, only **1.5625%** of the budget. | Usually near-zero decode gain; potentially small burst TTFT improvement. Budget fraction is **not** a speedup bound or prediction. A lower-MBT experiment would be a different arm. |
| 5 | **E10: host Engram allocation/placement** | Offload and DP sharing/sharding exist, but resolve the actual branch before choosing #59849, #59923 or #62359. Verify NUMA locality and allocator capabilities. | No defensible numeric serving estimate yet. Most plausible in prefill/host-memory stalls. Registration/NUMA branches differ; GB200 cuMem results are not H200 guarantees. |
| 6 | **E11/E14: prefix-group and final-rank locality** | Measure actual prefix misses per rank on agent-f75/sessions. API2 matters; endpoint affinity is already different from DP-rank affinity. | Could improve TTFT substantially on demonstrated misses; **zero expected benefit on the selected cache-isolated first diagnostic**. Do not adopt older-V4 patches unchanged. |
| 7 | **E12/E13: scheduler work and prefill alignment** | Measure host scheduling spans and rank skew under mixed prefill/decode. Revalidate source membership per patch. | Profile-dependent; no justified percentage yet. More likely to affect tails than short homogeneous decode. |
| 8 | **SM90 candidate-only indexer scoring, issue61830** | Real Hopper gap: candidate consumers compute dense logits then mask them. Existing SM100 sparse-MQA route cannot be enabled on H200. Needs an actual Hopper implementation. | Larger long-context ceiling, but poor first-test time-to-value. H20 report puts four consumer layers at **20% of a 1M-context step** at one tested load: even perfect removal implies at most **25% throughput** there before other effects. This says nothing comparable about 1K/8K traffic. |
| 9 | **E15/E18: fusion or alternate Hopper MoE/communication backend** | TP1 may expose useful fusion/communication changes; kernel and precision eligibility must be established first. Current MoE all-to-all config is `allgather_reducescatter`. | Potentially larger gains but integration, numerical and memory risk. Separate backend/precision/topology arms; no percentage justified from the current audit. |

Primary evidence: [#58818](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58818),
[#58984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58984),
[#61767](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61767),
[#59468](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59468),
[SM90 indexer request #61830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61830).
The remaining source links and restrictions are in the original experiment cards.

## Important Rejections

| Audit direction | H200 disposition |
|---|---|
| E01 / #61039 length-aware candidate selection | **Do not cherry-pick as a ready H200 win.** `has_deep_select()` in installed `sparse_mqa_logits.py:43` requires SM100. Upstream's length-aware route uses it; the fallback keeps full-width scoring/top-k. A Hopper port is separate work. |
| E06 / #60802 DeepSelect dispatch | Installed `IndexerTopKDispatcher` also gates DeepSelect to SM100. The proposed route is unavailable on this H200 build. |
| E03 / graph cap512 ->768/1024 and #62040 | **No immediate experiment at seq64.** Live startup captured target FULL(384 tokens,64 requests,q6) and draft FULL(320,64,q5). The specific largest-batch hole is absent. Reopen on runtime fallback or a later seq128 arm, not by copying B200 settings. |
| E05 MegaMoE JIT warmup | Separate startup objective; Blackwell MegaMoE patch is not a steady-state Hopper improvement. Existing startup was already in progress. |
| E08 packed MX activation chain, E09 B200 FlashMLA#227, SM100 routes in E18 | Not eligible as direct Hopper changes. These need architecture-specific ports or a different backend hypothesis. |
| E16 KV tier, E17 draft-context/adaptive changes | Offload tier is inactive; short-context pilot does not trigger long-draft degradation. Added features/output changes have lower first-experiment ROI. |

The source-level H200 exclusions are supported by the installed code and
[#61039's implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7c3f7e5500c85aacb72aab50bd1ce05485b1d73a/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py).
The graph-hole mechanism is documented in
[#62040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62040).

## Why #58818 First

The upstream H20 author reports +2.5% output TPS at C1 and +0.5% at C64, with
synthetic acceptance in the performance runs. We will use real rejection and
the actual H200 TP1/DP4 topology. Those differences limit transferability. The
upstream correctness runs used real verification, but their unit tests did
**not** exercise the newly shared-cache branch. Our candidate is unqualified
until that branch and actual decode behavior are checked.

For intuition, if duplicate plans cost 0.3 ms on a 15 ms critical-path step,
removing them saves 2% step latency and raises ideal throughput by about 2.04%.
The H200 planner count/time and exposed fraction must be measured. Neither
GPU bandwidth ratios nor the PR's microbenchmark multiplier predicts serving
throughput.

Keep a measured no-win outcome: a 0.5% effect below boot/run variation is a
reason to move to #58984, not to keep running until a favorable sample appears.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Use a separate mechanism diagnostic on actual invocation shapes to measure epilogue instructions, kernel duration and critical-path exposure. An instruction substitution without reduced exposed time rejects the proposed bottleneck explanation for that workload.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compare identical-input logits, masks and top-k sets before serving tests; then compare quality, exact output-token counts and all-rank draft/verify/accepted counters. Repeatability within one variant does not establish baseline equivalence.
alternatives.explanation: The changed arithmetic alters logits or top-k selections, producing a workload or quality change that masquerades as faster equivalent execution.

experiment.control: The attested baseline with its stock fmaxf contiguous epilogue, independently rebuilt using the same toolchain and launch configurations and equally JIT-warmed. This is the strongest evidenced static comparator; the packet establishes no equivalent flag or stronger drop-in implementation. Keep precision, scheduling, topology, speculation, telemetry and cache preparation identical.
experiment.correctness: Compare stock and treatment against an appropriate higher-precision reference, preserving masks, scale semantics and output dtype. Establish bounds for accumulators, weighted products, reductions and scale halving, including rounding and flush-to-zero behavior. Analytical objection, not an observed failure: finite positive FLT_MAX overflows when doubled; with unit weight and original scale 0.5, the original scalar contribution is finite while delayed compensation cannot recover it. Test extreme finite values, subnormal scales, signed zero, NaN and infinities, plus real-input distributions. Require downstream top-k-set agreement and ordering under the deployed tie policy, including near ties. Author-reported self-consistency is insufficient. Exercise applicable graph/eager, chunking, cache-hit/miss and distributed paths; run a quality subset because arithmetic changes. Map relevant G01–G05 once their definitions are available. Speculative acceptance is diagnostic, not a correctness score.
experiment.cost: Cheap first step: source/configuration/JIT-provenance inspection, followed only if warranted by a small isolated header port. Compilation, correctness and later GPU experiment costs are unknown; none were incurred here. With full eight-GPU node price P8 per hour, report cost per qualified output token as P8 × elapsed_seconds / (3600 × qualified_output_tokens). Keep P8 unset; do not transfer B200 pricing.
experiment.held_out_condition: Reserve distinct long-context lengths, ragged chunk boundaries, mixed prefill/decode arrivals and cold/warm prefix conditions without tuning on them. Keep the cache-isolated 1K/1K diagnostic separate from native anchors. Include paged-only execution as a negative control and verify actual residual contiguous work in warm-cache cases. Seq128 remains a separate configuration arm.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Active include/JIT provenance, numerical domain or dispatch cannot be established; zero hits lack adequate opportunity coverage; telemetry is missing; cache state or arrivals are unmatched; drift or intervals cannot resolve the useful-effect threshold; or only source-author microbenchmarks and profiled measurements are available. Unknown gates remain deferred, not qualified.
experiment.metrics: Primary: native agent-f75 8K/1K prefix workload and fixed-schedule Mooncake anchors adapted to seq64. Record TTFT distributions/tails, request TPOT=(last-first token time)/(server output tokens-1), exact tokens, throughput, qualified request goodput and replay lag. Record cached/uncached prompt tokens, KV blocks, preemption and all-rank draft/verify/accepted counter deltas, resets and missing coverage. Separately measure shape-specific kernel duration and exposed prefill time; exclude profiled runs from the serving frontier. Confirm small gains with at least five alternating paired full-run blocks, baseline-drift checks and paired uncertainty intervals; requests are not independent experimental units.
experiment.rejects_if: Adequate primary-workload coverage establishes that the changed kernel is unused or already equivalent; a supported-domain correctness failure has no acceptable remedy; or sufficiently precise paired results exclude the predeclared useful gain or show unacceptable quality, TTFT-tail, TPOT or goodput regressions. A microbenchmark win without primary serving value rejects promotion for this baseline.
experiment.supports_if: Active-artifact and numerical gates pass; eligible calls show the intended instruction change and reduced exposed prefill time; paired unprofiled primary runs show an improvement exceeding a predeclared practical threshold with uncertainty excluding no improvement, while quality and tail/TPOT guardrails pass. The effect follows eligible uncached work and weakens where verified cache hits remove it. A benefit confined to long-context diagnostics supports only that narrower applicability.
experiment.treatment: Future experiment only: follow attestation, activation, correctness, unprofiled screening, separate mechanism diagnosis, then paired confirmation and held-out evaluation. Change only the coupled three-line epilogue operation. Inspect generated SM90A code for the relevant FMNMX-to-FADD substitution, compensation and unexpected spills or instruction growth. Across every replica/rank, count patched-kernel hits over independently identified eligible contiguous-prefill call opportunities, reporting shapes and score volume; also report eligible calls over all prefill calls. Join requests to final ranks. Use equally warmed JIT artifacts with separately controlled cold KV prefixes and confirmed warm-prefix hits.

card.mechanism: Source proposal: replace fmaxf(x,0) with x+fabsf(x), then multiply each existing KV scale by 0.5. The author attributes improvement to replacing half-rate FMNMX with full-rate FADD using an absolute-value operand modifier. Transfer inference: this can shorten an exposed contiguous-prefill epilogue without changing scoring coverage or launch geometry. Instruction issue-rate improvement does not establish kernel or serving speedup. The separate paged kernel receives no direct optimization.

novelty.implementation: A narrow deployment port of an existing SM90 patch, with explicit numerical and JIT-provenance qualification.
novelty.nearest_prior_art: DeepGEMM #452 directly supplies the proposed optimization and attributes an analogous packed implementation to SM100. #303 concerns broader stores, staging and occupancy changes; its closure rationale is unknown.
novelty.scientific: No novelty claimed; this is an existing arithmetic and instruction-selection technique.
novelty.specific_delta: Replace the installed contiguous epilogue’s fmaxf transform and compensate both KV scales, while retaining the baseline’s launch settings and surrounding serving behavior.
novelty.workload: Evaluate exposure under native H200 seq64 agent-f75 and Mooncake traffic, using cold/warm discrimination to separate prefill savings from cache effects.

card.observed_bottleneck: None measured. Observed supplied source text retains the original transform and both uncompensated scale multiplications. The runtime snapshot configures prefix caching and chunked prefill but does not establish kernel dispatch. Author-reported results: H200, 132 SMs, SM90A; +4.8% kernel throughput for SQ=2048, SKV=8192, H=64, BF16, CP=1, and average +3.7% across 192 contiguous cases. The selected-shape measurements use best of three repetitions. These are neither independently reproduced observations nor serving gains; timing distributions, worst-case regressions, CP meaning and D for the 8K case are unknown.
card.predicted_direction: Conditionally lower contiguous-kernel duration and cold-prefill TTFT; possible throughput and parameterized cost improvements when this work limits service capacity. Direct paged-decode TPOT benefit is not predicted. Mixed-load TPOT may improve indirectly through reduced prefill interference. Warm-prefix benefit should diminish with removed eligible work. Effect sizes are unknown; zero benefit and regressions remain possible.
card.proposed_change: First inspect the pinned process’s import/include resolution, DeepGEMM revision, JIT cache provenance and contiguous-prefill call sites. The visible header lacks the change, but the executing implementation remains unknown. If eligible and absent, port only commit ee53a16b089d441cbfc4020cd558c1f05f623d97’s transform replacement and two half-scale folds into an isolated build, with a comment coupling the changes. Retain the stock build for rollback. Rebuild and identify affected JIT specializations; require numerical qualification before serving evaluation. If the supported input/scaling domain cannot justify the transformation, retain stock behavior rather than enabling it unconditionally.
card.revision_reason: Root editorial repair: expand the exact nine-character quote to satisfy the minimum quote length; mechanism, claims and experiment unchanged. Original rejection retained.
card.statement: Test a minimal port of DeepGEMM #452’s contiguous SM90 FP8 MQA epilogue into the pinned H200 build, conditional on proving active header use and a safe numerical domain. The supplied installed excerpt retains fmaxf and unhalved KV scales, establishing a source-level delta but no execution or bottleneck evidence. The PR author reports H200 microbenchmark gains from substituting full-rate FADD with an absolute-value operand and compensating both output scales. Our transfer hypothesis is lower exposed prefill time and TTFT where uncached requests invoke this kernel; warm-prefix and paged-only traffic should benefit little directly. Compare against the equally compiled, warmed stock epilogue at unchanged launch settings. Reject unconditional bit-exactness: overflow, underflow, exceptional values and downstream top-k stability must be resolved before serving tests. Serving value remains unmeasured.

policy.baseline_comparison: Use the supplied live attestation: vLLM ac9126e58aa7bbab1856ba6593ba4d5003fea516, serving checkout 11c249d28b2962f7384b4ab1fd7c1664704e7524, and the supplied image/model revision. Hardware is eight H200 SM90 GPUs, 143771 MiB each, arranged as two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas with API2 each. Preserve seq64, MBT16384, context1048576, graphcap512, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, embedding_across_dp, prefix caching, DSpark k5 probabilistic draft/block rejection, adaptive OFF, no-swa-bounded-replay and enabled telemetry except where explicitly varied. Primary comparisons preserve native agent-f75 8K/1K prefixes and fixed-schedule Mooncake anchors adapted to H200 seq64. Keep cache-isolated 1K/1K and long-context, ragged, mixed, cold/warm diagnostics separate. Seq128 is a separate arm. Verify attention/MoE dispatch and the reported allgather_reducescatter configuration; endpoint availability does not establish kernel activation.

criteria.description: REQUIRED VETO: Identify a credible, testable mechanism connecting the proposed change to task value, plus either a concrete baseline delta or an explicit cheap source/configuration/log inspection that determines whether the feature is already present and active. State the strongest simple comparator, including an existing flag or parameter adjustment where applicable. A demonstrated absence of both a useful delta and a credible improvement mechanism fails this gate. Unresolved baseline membership or bottleneck exposure defers judgment and motivates inspection; measured speedup is not required.
criteria.justification: The supplied baseline says, "No measured bottleneck or new GPU result." Several proposed directions may already exist or only matter under specific traffic. This receives the largest weight because useful incremental value, rather than publication status, is the selection objective.

criteria.description: REQUIRED VETO: Provide a plausible implementation, activation or explicit port path for SM90 and the pinned serving branches, with scoped correctness checks. Address relevant G01-G05 checks, numerical changes, graph/cache branches and distributed behavior; use a quality subset when math changes. Speculative acceptance is a diagnostic, not a correctness score. Demonstrated incompatibility or correctness failure without a credible remedy fails this gate. Unknown dispatch, branch membership or correctness remains deferred. An explicit Hopper port is eligible even when a direct SM100 activation is unavailable.
criteria.justification: The research must reopen B200 exclusions without assuming that Blackwell kernels, topology, precision paths or graph settings transfer to H200. Applicability and correctness are necessary gates, while implementation effort is assessed separately.

criteria.description: Specify the activation signal and eligible-opportunity denominator, competing explanations, strongest simple comparator, scoped correctness checks, held-out test and prospective support/reject/inconclusive rules. Follow attestation, activation, correctness, unprofiled screening, separate mechanism diagnosis, then paired confirmation and held-out evaluation. Use all-replica/rank coverage, request TPOT=(last-first token time)/(server output tokens-1), TTFT tails and relevant draft, KV, preemption, goodput or replay counters. Confirm small gains with at least five alternating paired full-run blocks, drift checks and intervals; avoid request-level pseudoreplication. Missing telemetry or inadequately covered zero hits is inconclusive. Exclude profiled measurements from the serving frontier.
criteria.justification: The evaluator contract is unusually specific, and likely effects may depend on padding, rank skew, prefix reuse or load. A discriminating experiment deserves substantial weight because it can expose a useful mechanism or cheaply falsify one without an existing bottleneck measurement.

criteria.description: Separate observed results, source-author claims, source fixes and transfer inference. Use short exact quotations and inspect the implementation or engineering artifact supporting the proposed mechanism. Record source hardware, workload, effect size and limitations as unknown whenever absent. Investigate negative results and branch/deployment restrictions. A paper abstract does not establish implementation behavior; prior ranking prose does not establish current source membership.
criteria.justification: No direct evidence accompanies this request. Traceability matters, but demanding multiple publications would unnecessarily exclude straightforward flag changes and small implementation fixes. One relevant engineering source can be sufficient.

criteria.description: Prefer inexpensive falsification, manageable integration and rollback, and benefits exposed by the primary workload. Identify when value is confined to a diagnostic regime. Consider memory pressure, quality, tail latency and throughput tradeoffs. Use parameterized eight-GPU node cost until H200 pricing is known. Across the five selections, favor complementary mechanisms and workload coverage to reduce redundant experiments, without requiring unpublished techniques.
criteria.justification: The requested output is a diverse, practical experiment shortlist. A cheap planner or scheduling change and a larger communication or long-context port can both merit consideration, but their integration costs, activation opportunities and learning value differ.

evidence.rationale: Require one directly relevant engineering source per supported selection, such as implementation code, a patch, a reproducible issue or a dispatch trace; multiple independent sources and papers are not universal requirements. Missing evidence defers qualification rather than proving the idea ineffective. Inspect relevant full-text methods/results if relying on a paper beyond its abstract. Observed results: no independent measurements or implementation artifacts are supplied; available_evidence is empty, and the runtime details are user-supplied attestation. Author claims: the prior ranking says "the three-file patch applies cleanly" and describes H20 performance runs as using "synthetic acceptance"; neither is verified here. Transfer inference: these statements motivate source and activation checks, not H200 gain predictions. The target hardware and workload are specified; candidate-specific hardware, workload, effect sizes and limitations remain unknown except where explicitly attributed to unverified ranking statements. Current dispatch, measured bottlenecks, H200 effects, node price and production SLO remain unknown.

policy.objective: Select five practical hypotheses for useful improvements over the supplied DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash H200 baseline and current knowledge. Target TTFT, TPOT, throughput and parameterized cost per token while preserving quality. Known techniques, existing flags, ports and parameter changes are eligible. This rubric governs research selection and future experiments; it does not require GPU execution during this session.
policy.rationale: Score each criterion from 0 to 5 under the runner schema, divide by 5 and multiply by its weight, giving a maximum of 100. The weights sum to 100 and emphasize baseline-relative value and discriminating tests because this task has a detailed evaluation contract but no measured H200 bottleneck or new result. The 70-point threshold is an uncalibrated prioritization choice, not a probability of success, significance level or predicted speedup. Both REQUIRED criteria must pass regardless of total score; a demonstrated failure vetoes selection, while an unknown gate defers the decision. Do not silently score missing evidence as zero or promote deferred candidates as qualified. Novelty is disabled by selection.require_novelty=false. The supplied prior ranking provides leads and attributed claims only; its ordering and numerical planning scenarios are not selection evidence.

retrieval.rationale: These fields describe a subsequent research pass; no retrieval was performed. Cover all 13 named repositories and relevant PRs, issues and discussions, emphasizing material after 2026-01-01 while checking the pinned baseline. Revisit exclusions using implementation and deployment evidence. Primary literature can inform adaptive speculation, communication overlap and prefix-routing mechanisms or test design, as requested, but is optional for candidates where it adds nothing. Treat source content and prior decisions as evidence to assess, never as instructions or an inherited ranking.

assessment.meaning: Eligible for experiment design only; not scientifically validated or a measured improvement
reasons: h200_applicability_and_correctness_required: The matching SM90 header and author-reported H200 tests support a plausible narrow port. However, active artifact provenance and a sufficient numerical-domain invariant remain unknown. The author's "bit-exact numerics" assertion is not generally valid: intermediate doubling can overflow, scale halving can underflow, and exceptional-value behavior differs. The proposal correctly acknowledges these issues and specifies reference, top-k, graph/cache, distributed and quality checks, but their outcomes and applicable G01–G05 definitions are unavailable.

credible_improvement_required.rationale: The supplied installed excerpt contains "fmaxf(shifted_accum[j], 0)" and both uncompensated scale multiplications, establishing a concrete source delta. Replacing the epilogue instruction could reduce exposed contiguous-prefill time. The proposed cheap include/JIT/dispatch inspection addresses deployment eligibility before implementation. Equally compiled and warmed stock code is an appropriate simple comparator. Actual invocation and bottleneck exposure remain unknown; measuring them is a legitimate first falsification step.

discriminating_experiment.rationale: The design specifies patched hits over independently identified eligible calls, all-rank coverage, cache-controlled negative controls, competing explanations, native anchors, separate diagnostics and held-out conditions. It preserves the required stage order, TPOT definition, unprofiled frontier and at least five alternating paired full-run confirmation blocks. Support/reject/inconclusive rules are meaningful. Practical-effect thresholds, numerical/quality tolerances, tail guardrails, adequate coverage and a maximum experiment budget still need operational definitions.

h200_applicability_and_correctness_requi.rationale: The matching SM90 header and author-reported H200 tests support a plausible narrow port. However, active artifact provenance and a sufficient numerical-domain invariant remain unknown. The author's "bit-exact numerics" assertion is not generally valid: intermediate doubling can overflow, scale halving can underflow, and exceptional-value behavior differs. The proposal correctly acknowledges these issues and specifies reference, top-k, graph/cache, distributed and quality checks, but their outcomes and applicable G01–G05 definitions are unavailable.

practical_value_and_portfolio_coverage.rationale: A conditional three-line header port offers inexpensive initial falsification and straightforward source rollback, although JIT artifact isolation must also be verified. Cold/warm discrimination addresses whether native prefix-heavy traffic exposes useful work. The proposal avoids claiming direct paged-decode gains and keeps eight-GPU node pricing parameterized. Integration effort and serving benefit remain unknown. Its prefill mechanism complements decode and routing directions, but five-selection portfolio coverage cannot be established from one submitted hypothesis.

traceable_engineering_support.rationale: Observed evidence is supplied source text, not measured execution. DeepGEMM #452 includes before/after code and author claims of H200 gains: "avg +3.7%" and selected-shape timing using "best of 3 reps". The draft correctly treats lower serving TTFT as transfer inference. It challenges universal exactness and records missing distributions, worst-case regressions, CP meaning and the 8K case's D as unknown. The #303 slowdown anecdote is appropriately contextualized; neither its cause nor closure rationale establishes rejection of #452.

objections: An unchanged installed header does not prove the serving process executes it. Include resolution, loaded dependencies, JIT cache provenance and eligible invocation coverage must establish the effective baseline.

Finite accumulator observations alone cannot qualify the arithmetic. Bounds must cover doubled accumulators, weighted products, intermediate reductions and halved scales under actual compiler rounding and flush-to-zero behavior. The scalar overflow counterexample challenges universal equivalence; it does not establish a failure on reachable deployment inputs.

The highlighted 8K author benchmark uses BF16 logits. Supplied vLLM #61149 states "SM90 and SM120 keep the FP8 format, FP32 weights and FP32 logits." That is an attributed branch-description claim, not proof of pinned deployment membership, but it makes dtype and compressed-row API matching an explicit transfer question.

Kernel throughput gains cannot establish primary-workload TTFT or goodput gains. Prefix reuse, other prefill stages and contention may remove the exposed benefit; the proposed controls appropriately test these alternatives.
The experiment's decision thresholds and stopping budget remain unspecified. Five paired blocks are a minimum design requirement, not assurance that a small effect will be resolved.
