prior_decision_text.runs/pr-evaluation-audit-001/h200/RANKIN:
# H200 experiment order

Assessed 2026-10-20 against the running eight-H200 node. These are **untested
H200 hypotheses**. Rank means expected learning/useful improvement per unit of
integration and GPU time. It does not mean largest possible eventual speedup.
Numerical ranges below are engineering planning scenarios, not measurements or
confidence intervals; zero and regressions remain possible.

## Actual scope

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`.
- Two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas; API2 each; eight H200s total.
- vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev493+gac9126e58`, image `sha256:3d17635c5aa0340e2f2502c067ce4b587d8e7dc678195e90b71142490dc6d71c`.
- Installed serving checkout `11c249d28b2962f7384b4ab1fd7c1664704e7524`, branch
  `more_metrics`. This is newer than the audit's serving snapshot.
- **64 sequences per DP engine**, not the audit's 128-sequence R7b override.
  MBT16384, context1048576, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, prefix cache enabled,
  real DSpark k5/block rejection/adaptive OFF. Verbose request/output/delta
  logging and graph/speculation metrics are enabled. Keep these identical in A/B.
- H200 is SM90; the audit's MegaAttention/MegaMoE/SM100 assumptions do not carry
  over. `nvidia-smi` reports 143771 MiB per GPU and driver580.126.20.

## Ranked Queue

| Rank | Candidate | H200 validity and cheapest falsification | Potential end-to-end delta and effort |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Share FlashMLA plans, PR58818**; reopened B200 exclusion | Installed MRV2/SWA code creates per-group holders, and the three-file patch applies cleanly. Same SM90 mechanism has H20 evidence. Verify redundant planner launches on this TP1/DP4 path; TP8's exact counts are not guaranteed. | Planning range: **0-3% lower low-load decode TPOT**, often **0-1% at saturation**. Three Python files, no dependency rebuild. Best first cheap test, modest ceiling. |
| 2 | **E02: logical drafter rows, PR58984** | Installed `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync` uses target graph capacity (`target_dp_sync.num_reqs`). With adaptive OFF, count real requests versus padded drafter rows under ragged arrivals. Stop if equal. | **0-10%** is a broad test scenario only where padding wastes material work; likely near zero at aligned full batches. Four-file patch, DP correctness tests and an older-base port review. |
| 3 | **E04: CPU DP collectives, PR61767** | New `cpu_all_reduce_` is absent in inspected installed files. Both replicas synchronize four DP ranks. Measure exposed CPU collective time, excluding rank-arrival skew. | **0-5%** scenario if dispatch gaps dominate; zero if hidden by GPU work. More distributed correctness risk than #1. No kernel/toolchain rebuild expected. |
| 4 | **E07: draft token-budget accounting, PR59468** | Check reservations and budget-limited prefill admission at existing MBT16384. Real bound here is **64*(5-1)=256 tokens/rank**, only **1.5625%** of the budget. | Usually near-zero decode gain; potentially small burst TTFT improvement. Budget fraction is **not** a speedup bound or prediction. A lower-MBT experiment would be a different arm. |
| 5 | **E10: host Engram allocation/placement** | Offload and DP sharing/sharding exist, but resolve the actual branch before choosing #59849, #59923 or #62359. Verify NUMA locality and allocator capabilities. | No defensible numeric serving estimate yet. Most plausible in prefill/host-memory stalls. Registration/NUMA branches differ; GB200 cuMem results are not H200 guarantees. |
| 6 | **E11/E14: prefix-group and final-rank locality** | Measure actual prefix misses per rank on agent-f75/sessions. API2 matters; endpoint affinity is already different from DP-rank affinity. | Could improve TTFT substantially on demonstrated misses; **zero expected benefit on the selected cache-isolated first diagnostic**. Do not adopt older-V4 patches unchanged. |
| 7 | **E12/E13: scheduler work and prefill alignment** | Measure host scheduling spans and rank skew under mixed prefill/decode. Revalidate source membership per patch. | Profile-dependent; no justified percentage yet. More likely to affect tails than short homogeneous decode. |
| 8 | **SM90 candidate-only indexer scoring, issue61830** | Real Hopper gap: candidate consumers compute dense logits then mask them. Existing SM100 sparse-MQA route cannot be enabled on H200. Needs an actual Hopper implementation. | Larger long-context ceiling, but poor first-test time-to-value. H20 report puts four consumer layers at **20% of a 1M-context step** at one tested load: even perfect removal implies at most **25% throughput** there before other effects. This says nothing comparable about 1K/8K traffic. |
| 9 | **E15/E18: fusion or alternate Hopper MoE/communication backend** | TP1 may expose useful fusion/communication changes; kernel and precision eligibility must be established first. Current MoE all-to-all config is `allgather_reducescatter`. | Potentially larger gains but integration, numerical and memory risk. Separate backend/precision/topology arms; no percentage justified from the current audit. |

Primary evidence: [#58818](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58818),
[#58984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58984),
[#61767](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61767),
[#59468](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59468),
[SM90 indexer request #61830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61830).
The remaining source links and restrictions are in the original experiment cards.

## Important Rejections

| Audit direction | H200 disposition |
|---|---|
| E01 / #61039 length-aware candidate selection | **Do not cherry-pick as a ready H200 win.** `has_deep_select()` in installed `sparse_mqa_logits.py:43` requires SM100. Upstream's length-aware route uses it; the fallback keeps full-width scoring/top-k. A Hopper port is separate work. |
| E06 / #60802 DeepSelect dispatch | Installed `IndexerTopKDispatcher` also gates DeepSelect to SM100. The proposed route is unavailable on this H200 build. |
| E03 / graph cap512 ->768/1024 and #62040 | **No immediate experiment at seq64.** Live startup captured target FULL(384 tokens,64 requests,q6) and draft FULL(320,64,q5). The specific largest-batch hole is absent. Reopen on runtime fallback or a later seq128 arm, not by copying B200 settings. |
| E05 MegaMoE JIT warmup | Separate startup objective; Blackwell MegaMoE patch is not a steady-state Hopper improvement. Existing startup was already in progress. |
| E08 packed MX activation chain, E09 B200 FlashMLA#227, SM100 routes in E18 | Not eligible as direct Hopper changes. These need architecture-specific ports or a different backend hypothesis. |
| E16 KV tier, E17 draft-context/adaptive changes | Offload tier is inactive; short-context pilot does not trigger long-draft degradation. Added features/output changes have lower first-experiment ROI. |

The source-level H200 exclusions are supported by the installed code and
[#61039's implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7c3f7e5500c85aacb72aab50bd1ce05485b1d73a/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py).
The graph-hole mechanism is documented in
[#62040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62040).

## Why #58818 First

The upstream H20 author reports +2.5% output TPS at C1 and +0.5% at C64, with
synthetic acceptance in the performance runs. We will use real rejection and
the actual H200 TP1/DP4 topology. Those differences limit transferability. The
upstream correctness runs used real verification, but their unit tests did
**not** exercise the newly shared-cache branch. Our candidate is unqualified
until that branch and actual decode behavior are checked.

For intuition, if duplicate plans cost 0.3 ms on a 15 ms critical-path step,
removing them saves 2% step latency and raises ideal throughput by about 2.04%.
The H200 planner count/time and exposed fraction must be measured. Neither
GPU bandwidth ratios nor the PR's microbenchmark multiplier predicts serving
throughput.

Keep a measured no-win outcome: a 0.5% effect below boot/run variation is a
reason to move to #58984, not to keep running until a favorable sample appears.

experiment.correctness: Run relevant G01–G05 after obtaining their definitions. Verify dispatch/combine token identity, routing weights, scale metadata, duplicate destinations, zero-token ranks, ragged batches, buffer sizing/alignment, repeated wraparound, and maximum supported graph tiers. Establish the three-buffer/store-group lifetime invariant and host/device sizing agreement; stress graph capture/replay and collective ordering. Preserve DSpark rejection and KV rollback. If reduction order changes, assess numerical and paired quality effects. The closed Hopper issue reports a workaround removing DeepEP, not a demonstrated fix.
experiment.cost: Compatibility inspection is cheap; an elastic adapter and buffer/graph validation may require substantial integration work, with effort unknown. Stop before GPU testing if no comparable path exists. No execution in this run. Parameterize full-node cost as P8*T/(3600*N_out), with P8 unknown, and report qualified-output cost separately.
experiment.held_out_condition: Separate cold/warm 1K/1K diagnostics, long-context mixed prefill/decode, ragged arrivals, empty and uneven ranks, local-heavy routing, and skewed expert demand. Exercise both EP4 groups concurrently; keep seq128 separate.
experiment.inconclusive_if: The engine reaches another DeepEP implementation, telemetry or remote-traffic coverage is inadequate, the buffer invariant is unresolved, compute/format changes remain confounded, or only remote-only bandwidth improves. Wide intervals and substantial baseline drift also remain inconclusive.
experiment.metrics: All-rank direct-NVLink and triple-buffer path hits divided by eligible MoE dispatch invocations, with remote routed rows/bytes as additional exposure denominators. Record local traffic fraction, per-rank expert counts, message sizes, dispatch/combine time, exposed critical-path time, shared memory, occupancy, and graph fallbacks. Serving metrics: request TPOT=(last-first token time)/(server output tokens-1), TTFT tails, exact tokens, throughput, qualified goodput, replay lag, draft/verify/accepted deltas, KV blocks, preemption, and failures.
experiment.rejects_if: Inspection establishes no useful delta, incompatible transport/compute contracts lack a credible remedy, synchronization correctness fails, or adequately precise primary-workload comparisons rule out practical improvement. A patch that improves B but still loses to A is not a baseline deployment improvement.
experiment.supports_if: C beats the strongest unmodified DeepEP comparator with verified pipeline activation and reduced exposed dispatch time; and C also improves over A on a predeclared primary workload beyond the useful-gain margin without quality or latency guardrail violations. Report backend activation and patch effects separately.
experiment.treatment: First inspect effective source/config/logs, NVLink placement, adapter/API compatibility, and whether #693 is already included. Stage A versus B isolates backend activation; B versus C isolates triple buffering. Establish activation and correctness before unprofiled agent-f75 and fixed-schedule Mooncake screening. Diagnose communication separately with profiling, then confirm useful small effects using at least five alternating paired full-run blocks, drift checks, and run-level intervals. Do not combine this arm with SGLang migration or numeric changes.

card.mechanism: Source code/review exposes three staging buffers and partial store-group waiting. Transfer inference: overlapping next-token loads and metadata preparation with prior remote stores can reduce serialized dispatch time. Increased shared-memory demand and the dispatch-warp cap can offset savings through occupancy loss or contention with expert computation.

novelty.implementation: Conditional integration of elastic direct-NVLink dispatch into the pinned engine, followed by an isolated upstream pipeline port.

novelty.scientific: Known communication pipelining; no novelty claim.

novelty.workload: Four-rank mixed-locality EP serving with real DSpark and native prefix traffic, unlike the source's eight-rank remote-only bandwidth test.

card.observed_bottleneck: No target communication bottleneck is measured. The supplied startup excerpt selects Marlin; the reported allgather_reducescatter transport remains unverified. Author report: #693 raises average eight-H100 dispatch bandwidth from 250 to 280 GB/s, and 203 to 220 GB/s under imbalance ratio 1.5; combine is unchanged. Tests ignore local traffic. Payload dimensions, numeric format, repetitions, variance, and H200 serving effects are unknown.
card.predicted_direction: Potentially lower exposed dispatch latency and improved TPOT or throughput when remote dispatch is material. Combine has no source-reported improvement. Zero benefit or regression is plausible for local-heavy traffic, small batches, or resource contention; no H200 effect size is predicted.
card.proposed_change: First establish transport and API compatibility. If feasible, integrate unmodified elastic direct-NVLink DeepEP while holding Marlin, routing semantics, payload format, topology, and speculation fixed. Then port only #693's pipeline with one shared host/device buffer-count definition and a verified reuse invariant. Preserve rollback to the original backend. If compute or activation format must change, separate that prerequisite rather than labeling the result communication-only.
card.revision_reason: Unchanged mechanism reconsidered under this task and policy; original decision retained
card.statement: Test direct-NVLink DeepEP dispatch in two attributable stages: compatible backend activation, followed by the triple-buffered prefetch change in #693. First verify the effective baseline transport, four-rank NVLink connectivity, and whether the pinned engine can reach the elastic direct-NVLink implementation while preserving Marlin and its activation payload. The supplied patch overlaps preparation of the next token with outstanding remote stores, but its positive evidence is an eight-H100, remote-only bandwidth test. Four-rank serving may have more local traffic, smaller messages, and greater resource contention. Compare unmodified DeepEP with the baseline before comparing patched and unmodified DeepEP at fixed compute and numeric settings. Resolve the buffer-lifetime invariant and graph behavior before performance testing. Historical mixed-configuration regressions motivate these controls but do not establish that DeepEP will lose here.

Hardware is eight H200 SM90 GPUs, 143771 MiB each, arranged as two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas with API2 each. Preserve seq64, MBT16384, context1048576, graphcap512, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, embedding_across_dp, prefix caching, DSpark k5 probabilistic draft/block rejection, adaptive OFF, no-swa-bounded-replay and enabled telemetry except where explicitly varied. Primary comparisons preserve native agent-f75 8K/1K prefixes and fixed-schedule Mooncake anchors adapted to H200 seq64. Keep cache-isolated 1K/1K and long-context, ragged, mixed, cold/warm diagnostics separate. Seq128 is a separate arm. criteria.description: REQUIRED VETO: Identify a credible, testable mechanism connecting the proposed change to task value, plus either a concrete baseline delta or an explicit cheap source/configuration/log inspection that determines whether the feature is already present and active. State the strongest simple comparator, including an existing flag or parameter adjustment where applicable. A demonstrated absence of both a useful delta and a credible improvement mechanism fails this gate. Unresolved baseline membership or bottleneck exposure defers judgment and motivates inspection; measured speedup is not required.
criteria.justification: The supplied baseline says, "No measured bottleneck or new GPU result." Several proposed directions may already exist or only matter under specific traffic. This receives the largest weight because useful incremental value, rather than publication status, is the selection objective.

criteria.description: REQUIRED VETO: Provide a plausible implementation, activation or explicit port path for SM90 and the pinned serving branches, with scoped correctness checks. Address relevant G01-G05 checks, numerical changes, graph/cache branches and distributed behavior; use a quality subset when math changes. Speculative acceptance is a diagnostic, not a correctness score. Demonstrated incompatibility or correctness failure without a credible remedy fails this gate. Unknown dispatch, branch membership or correctness remains deferred. An explicit Hopper port is eligible even when a direct SM100 activation is unavailable.
criteria.justification: The research must reopen B200 exclusions without assuming that Blackwell kernels, topology, precision paths or graph settings transfer to H200. Applicability and correctness are necessary gates, while implementation effort is assessed separately.

criteria.description: Specify the activation signal and eligible-opportunity denominator, competing explanations, strongest simple comparator, scoped correctness checks, held-out test and prospective support/reject/inconclusive rules. Follow attestation, activation, correctness, unprofiled screening, separate mechanism diagnosis, then paired confirmation and held-out evaluation. Use all-replica/rank coverage, request TPOT=(last-first token time)/(server output tokens-1), TTFT tails and relevant draft, KV, preemption, goodput or replay counters. Confirm small gains with at least five alternating paired full-run blocks, drift checks and intervals; avoid request-level pseudoreplication. Missing telemetry or inadequately covered zero hits is inconclusive. Exclude profiled measurements from the serving frontier.
criteria.justification: The evaluator contract is unusually specific, and likely effects may depend on padding, rank skew, prefix reuse or load. A discriminating experiment deserves substantial weight because it can expose a useful mechanism or cheaply falsify one without an existing bottleneck measurement.

criteria.description: Separate observed results, source-author claims, source fixes and transfer inference. Use short exact quotations and inspect the implementation or engineering artifact supporting the proposed mechanism. Record source hardware, workload, effect size and limitations as unknown whenever absent. Investigate negative results and branch/deployment restrictions. A paper abstract does not establish implementation behavior; prior ranking prose does not establish current source membership.
criteria.justification: No direct evidence accompanies this request. Traceability matters, but demanding multiple publications would unnecessarily exclude straightforward flag changes and small implementation fixes. One relevant engineering source can be sufficient.

criteria.description: Prefer inexpensive falsification, manageable integration and rollback, and benefits exposed by the primary workload. Identify when value is confined to a diagnostic regime. Consider memory pressure, quality, tail latency and throughput tradeoffs. Use parameterized eight-GPU node cost until H200 pricing is known. Across the five selections, favor complementary mechanisms and workload coverage to reduce redundant experiments, without requiring unpublished techniques.
criteria.justification: The requested output is a diverse, practical experiment shortlist. A cheap planner or scheduling change and a larger communication or long-context port can both merit consideration, but their integration costs, activation opportunities and learning value differ.

evidence.rationale: Require one directly relevant engineering source per supported selection, such as implementation code, a patch, a reproducible issue or a dispatch trace; multiple independent sources and papers are not universal requirements. Missing evidence defers qualification rather than proving the idea ineffective. Inspect relevant full-text methods/results if relying on a paper beyond its abstract. Observed results: no independent measurements or implementation artifacts are supplied; available_evidence is empty, and the runtime details are user-supplied attestation. Author claims: the prior ranking says "the three-file patch applies cleanly" and describes H20 performance runs as using "synthetic acceptance"; neither is verified here. Transfer inference: these statements motivate source and activation checks, not H200 gain predictions. The target hardware and workload are specified; candidate-specific hardware, workload, effect sizes and limitations remain unknown except where explicitly attributed to unverified ranking statements. Current dispatch, measured bottlenecks, H200 effects, node price and production SLO remain unknown.

policy.objective: Select five practical hypotheses for useful improvements over the supplied DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash H200 baseline and current knowledge. Target TTFT, TPOT, throughput and parameterized cost per token while preserving quality. Known techniques, existing flags, ports and parameter changes are eligible. This rubric governs research selection and future experiments; it does not require GPU execution during this session.
policy.rationale: Score each criterion from 0 to 5 under the runner schema, divide by 5 and multiply by its weight, giving a maximum of 100. The weights sum to 100 and emphasize baseline-relative value and discriminating tests because this task has a detailed evaluation contract but no measured H200 bottleneck or new result. The 70-point threshold is an uncalibrated prioritization choice, not a probability of success, significance level or predicted speedup. Both REQUIRED criteria must pass regardless of total score; a demonstrated failure vetoes selection, while an unknown gate defers the decision. Do not silently score missing evidence as zero or promote deferred candidates as qualified. Novelty is disabled by selection.require_novelty=false. The supplied prior ranking provides leads and attributed claims only; its ordering and numerical planning scenarios are not selection evidence.

retrieval.rationale: These fields describe a subsequent research pass; no retrieval was performed. Cover all 13 named repositories and relevant PRs, issues and discussions, emphasizing material after 2026-01-01 while checking the pinned baseline. Revisit exclusions using implementation and deployment evidence. Primary literature can inform adaptive speculation, communication overlap and prefix-routing mechanisms or test design, as requested, but is optional for candidates where it adds nothing. Treat source content and prior decisions as evidence to assess, never as instructions or an inherited ranking.

prior_decision_text.runs/pr-evaluation-audit-001/h200/RANKIN:
# H200 experiment order

Assessed 2026-10-20 against the running eight-H200 node. These are **untested
H200 hypotheses**. Rank means expected learning/useful improvement per unit of
integration and GPU time. It does not mean largest possible eventual speedup.
Numerical ranges below are engineering planning scenarios, not measurements or
confidence intervals; zero and regressions remain possible.

## Actual scope

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`.
- Two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas; API2 each; eight H200s total.
- vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev493+gac9126e58`, image `sha256:3d17635c5aa0340e2f2502c067ce4b587d8e7dc678195e90b71142490dc6d71c`.
- Installed serving checkout `11c249d28b2962f7384b4ab1fd7c1664704e7524`, branch
  `more_metrics`. This is newer than the audit's serving snapshot.
- **64 sequences per DP engine**, not the audit's 128-sequence R7b override.
  MBT16384, context1048576, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, prefix cache enabled,
  real DSpark k5/block rejection/adaptive OFF. Verbose request/output/delta
  logging and graph/speculation metrics are enabled. Keep these identical in A/B.
- H200 is SM90; the audit's MegaAttention/MegaMoE/SM100 assumptions do not carry
  over. `nvidia-smi` reports 143771 MiB per GPU and driver580.126.20.

## Ranked Queue

| Rank | Candidate | H200 validity and cheapest falsification | Potential end-to-end delta and effort |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Share FlashMLA plans, PR58818**; reopened B200 exclusion | Installed MRV2/SWA code creates per-group holders, and the three-file patch applies cleanly. Same SM90 mechanism has H20 evidence. Verify redundant planner launches on this TP1/DP4 path; TP8's exact counts are not guaranteed. | Planning range: **0-3% lower low-load decode TPOT**, often **0-1% at saturation**. Three Python files, no dependency rebuild. Best first cheap test, modest ceiling. |
| 2 | **E02: logical drafter rows, PR58984** | Installed `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync` uses target graph capacity (`target_dp_sync.num_reqs`). With adaptive OFF, count real requests versus padded drafter rows under ragged arrivals. Stop if equal. | **0-10%** is a broad test scenario only where padding wastes material work; likely near zero at aligned full batches. Four-file patch, DP correctness tests and an older-base port review. |
| 3 | **E04: CPU DP collectives, PR61767** | New `cpu_all_reduce_` is absent in inspected installed files. Both replicas synchronize four DP ranks. Measure exposed CPU collective time, excluding rank-arrival skew. | **0-5%** scenario if dispatch gaps dominate; zero if hidden by GPU work. More distributed correctness risk than #1. No kernel/toolchain rebuild expected. |
| 4 | **E07: draft token-budget accounting, PR59468** | Check reservations and budget-limited prefill admission at existing MBT16384. Real bound here is **64*(5-1)=256 tokens/rank**, only **1.5625%** of the budget. | Usually near-zero decode gain; potentially small burst TTFT improvement. Budget fraction is **not** a speedup bound or prediction. A lower-MBT experiment would be a different arm. |
| 5 | **E10: host Engram allocation/placement** | Offload and DP sharing/sharding exist, but resolve the actual branch before choosing #59849, #59923 or #62359. Verify NUMA locality and allocator capabilities. | No defensible numeric serving estimate yet. Most plausible in prefill/host-memory stalls. Registration/NUMA branches differ; GB200 cuMem results are not H200 guarantees. |
| 6 | **E11/E14: prefix-group and final-rank locality** | Measure actual prefix misses per rank on agent-f75/sessions. API2 matters; endpoint affinity is already different from DP-rank affinity. | Could improve TTFT substantially on demonstrated misses; **zero expected benefit on the selected cache-isolated first diagnostic**. Do not adopt older-V4 patches unchanged. |
| 7 | **E12/E13: scheduler work and prefill alignment** | Measure host scheduling spans and rank skew under mixed prefill/decode. Revalidate source membership per patch. | Profile-dependent; no justified percentage yet. More likely to affect tails than short homogeneous decode. |
| 8 | **SM90 candidate-only indexer scoring, issue61830** | Real Hopper gap: candidate consumers compute dense logits then mask them. Existing SM100 sparse-MQA route cannot be enabled on H200. Needs an actual Hopper implementation. | Larger long-context ceiling, but poor first-test time-to-value. H20 report puts four consumer layers at **20% of a 1M-context step** at one tested load: even perfect removal implies at most **25% throughput** there before other effects. This says nothing comparable about 1K/8K traffic. |
| 9 | **E15/E18: fusion or alternate Hopper MoE/communication backend** | TP1 may expose useful fusion/communication changes; kernel and precision eligibility must be established first. Current MoE all-to-all config is `allgather_reducescatter`. | Potentially larger gains but integration, numerical and memory risk. Separate backend/precision/topology arms; no percentage justified from the current audit. |

Primary evidence: [#58818](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58818),
[#58984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58984),
[#61767](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61767),
[#59468](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59468),
[SM90 indexer request #61830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61830).
The remaining source links and restrictions are in the original experiment cards.

## Important Rejections

| Audit direction | H200 disposition |
|---|---|
| E01 / #61039 length-aware candidate selection | **Do not cherry-pick as a ready H200 win.** `has_deep_select()` in installed `sparse_mqa_logits.py:43` requires SM100. Upstream's length-aware route uses it; the fallback keeps full-width scoring/top-k. A Hopper port is separate work. |
| E06 / #60802 DeepSelect dispatch | Installed `IndexerTopKDispatcher` also gates DeepSelect to SM100. The proposed route is unavailable on this H200 build. |
| E03 / graph cap512 ->768/1024 and #62040 | **No immediate experiment at seq64.** Live startup captured target FULL(384 tokens,64 requests,q6) and draft FULL(320,64,q5). The specific largest-batch hole is absent. Reopen on runtime fallback or a later seq128 arm, not by copying B200 settings. |
| E05 MegaMoE JIT warmup | Separate startup objective; Blackwell MegaMoE patch is not a steady-state Hopper improvement. Existing startup was already in progress. |
| E08 packed MX activation chain, E09 B200 FlashMLA#227, SM100 routes in E18 | Not eligible as direct Hopper changes. These need architecture-specific ports or a different backend hypothesis. |
| E16 KV tier, E17 draft-context/adaptive changes | Offload tier is inactive; short-context pilot does not trigger long-draft degradation. Added features/output changes have lower first-experiment ROI. |

The source-level H200 exclusions are supported by the installed code and
[#61039's implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7c3f7e5500c85aacb72aab50bd1ce05485b1d73a/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py).
The graph-hole mechanism is documented in
[#62040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62040).

## Why #58818 First

The upstream H20 author reports +2.5% output TPS at C1 and +0.5% at C64, with
synthetic acceptance in the performance runs. We will use real rejection and
the actual H200 TP1/DP4 topology. Those differences limit transferability. The
upstream correctness runs used real verification, but their unit tests did
**not** exercise the newly shared-cache branch. Our candidate is unqualified
until that branch and actual decode behavior are checked.

For intuition, if duplicate plans cost 0.3 ms on a 15 ms critical-path step,
removing them saves 2% step latency and raises ideal throughput by about 2.04%.
The H200 planner count/time and exposed fraction must be measured. Neither
GPU bandwidth ratios nor the PR's microbenchmark multiplier predicts serving
throughput.

Keep a measured no-win outcome: a 0.5% effect below boot/run variation is a
reason to move to #58984, not to keep running until a favorable sample appears.

target.gpu: 8x NVIDIA H200 SM90, 143771 MiB per GPU
target.topology: two independent four-GPU TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas, API2 each
target.workload: Preserve native agent-f75 8K/1K prefix workload and fixed-schedule Mooncake anchors, adapted explicitly to H200 seq64; separate 1K/1K cache-isolated diagnostic and long-context, ragged, mixed, cold/warm held-out diagnostics.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Inspect the dependency graph and measure useful overlap with TP1 unchanged. Reject this topology-specific mechanism if coefficient consumers cannot proceed concurrently with independent work.
alternatives.explanation: At TP1 there is insufficient independent work, and the apparent opportunity depends on TP communication.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compare complete mHC boundaries against the best validated synchronous configuration, including H200-COMP-003 if successful; measure extra launches, waits, and interference.
alternatives.explanation: The synchronous fused operation is faster than overlapping a less-fused path.

card.applicability: Deferred, higher-risk port. The exact TP1 dependency window must be established. #60768 has no supplied Hopper GPU validation. SGLang #41251 reports a multi-operator bundle on H200 TP8/EP1; it supplies no overlap ablation. #60777's later H20 failure challenges the compensated-BF16 implementation, which is excluded here.
card.code_surface: vllm/config/kernel.py; vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/mhc.py; tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_dispatch.py and test_mhc_kernels.py. Separate prerequisite: packaged sm90_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm.cuh and its generated/cached artifact.

evidence.quote: These mock capability checks validate dispatch only.
There is no throughput improvement claim for this correctness repair.
The current implementation is not a performance win in the tested shapes, and its original numerical suite is not fully passing.

experiment.control: Best validated synchronous fused mHC at fixed arithmetic, plus a corrected-baseline reference if the TF32 repair is required. Preserve the supplied deployment and native agent-f75/Mooncake traffic. Use identical repaired artifacts in both performance arms.
experiment.correctness: Verify the register-lifetime repair in the actual generated artifact; run independent FP32/FP64 references and repeated calls across split-K, PDL and side streams. Check stream ordering, changed-input graph replay, cache/configuration hashing, and fallback behavior with GPU synchronization diagnostics. Run model quality with real DSpark. Kernel repeatability does not establish whole-model token determinism.
experiment.cost: Moderate-to-high integration and correctness cost; stop before GPU work if the dependency window is absent. Future full-node cost is P8*T_hours/N_valid_output_tokens; price and duration are unknown.
experiment.held_out_condition: Ragged rank arrivals, mixed prefill/decode, long contexts, cold/warm prefixes, empty ranks, and batches around the overlap threshold; separately exercise eager, piecewise, and large-batch fallbacks.
experiment.inconclusive_if: The executed TF32 artifact is unidentified, graph replay is unvalidated, eligible opportunities are sparse, or intervals remain broad. CPU dispatch tests and auxiliary-stream launches alone are insufficient.
experiment.metrics: Count overlap launches over opportunities passing all non-architecture guards, and report eligible opportunities/all coefficient operations. Distinguish stream activity from useful concurrent execution and exposed waits. Across all ranks measure request TPOT=(last-first)/(output_tokens-1), TTFT tails, exact throughput, goodput/replay lag, KV/preemption, and draft/verify/accepted deltas.
experiment.rejects_if: No legal TP1 overlap window exists, the port has an unrepaired stream/numerical failure, or sufficiently precise measurements show overhead and contention eliminate useful improvement.
experiment.supports_if: Useful overlap reduces the complete critical path and improves a prespecified serving metric over the strongest synchronous comparator without quality or tail regressions. Confirm small gains with at least five alternating paired full-run blocks, drift checks, and run-level intervals.
experiment.treatment: First establish dependencies, source applicability, and artifact correctness. Then enable only SM90 overlap, verify activation and numerical/graph behavior, screen unprofiled, diagnose overlap separately, and confirm serving results. Retain synchronous fallback and the initial sixteen-token threshold.

card.mechanism: Schedule dependency-independent coefficient work on an auxiliary stream so some latency is hidden. Additional launches, synchronization, contention, or lost post/pre fusion can outweigh that saving.

novelty.implementation: Qualify an existing experimental Hopper opt-in while retaining TF32 arithmetic.

card.statement: Test the existing mHC coefficient-stream overlap design on SM90 through an explicit opt-in, after repairing and validating any executed TF32 prenorm path. Installed source excludes SM90, while #60768 describes a constrained opt-in with CPU dispatch tests only. The proposed performance mechanism is to hide independent coefficient work behind other GPU work; at TP1, it cannot claim a fused TP all-reduce saving. First establish a legal overlap window and compare against the best validated synchronous fused mHC configuration. SGLang's bundled improvements do not isolate overlap, and the failed compensated-BF16 port supplies no reason to change arithmetic. Benefits, contention costs, and the suitability of the inherited sixteen-token threshold are unknown.

criteria.description: REQUIRED VETO: Identify a credible, testable mechanism connecting the proposed change to task value, plus either a concrete baseline delta or an explicit cheap source/configuration/log inspection that determines whether the feature is already present and active. State the strongest simple comparator, including an existing flag or parameter adjustment where applicable. A demonstrated absence of both a useful delta and a credible improvement mechanism fails this gate. Unresolved baseline membership or bottleneck exposure defers judgment and motivates inspection; measured speedup is not required.
criteria.justification: The supplied baseline says, "No measured bottleneck or new GPU result." Several proposed directions may already exist or only matter under specific traffic. This receives the largest weight because useful incremental value, rather than publication status, is the selection objective.

criteria.description: REQUIRED VETO: Provide a plausible implementation, activation or explicit port path for SM90 and the pinned serving branches, with scoped correctness checks. Address relevant G01-G05 checks, numerical changes, graph/cache branches and distributed behavior; use a quality subset when math changes. Speculative acceptance is a diagnostic, not a correctness score. Demonstrated incompatibility or correctness failure without a credible remedy fails this gate. Unknown dispatch, branch membership or correctness remains deferred. An explicit Hopper port is eligible even when a direct SM100 activation is unavailable.
criteria.justification: The research must reopen B200 exclusions without assuming that Blackwell kernels, topology, precision paths or graph settings transfer to H200. Applicability and correctness are necessary gates, while implementation effort is assessed separately.

criteria.description: Specify the activation signal and eligible-opportunity denominator, competing explanations, strongest simple comparator, scoped correctness checks, held-out test and prospective support/reject/inconclusive rules. Follow attestation, activation, correctness, unprofiled screening, separate mechanism diagnosis, then paired confirmation and held-out evaluation. Use all-replica/rank coverage, request TPOT=(last-first token time)/(server output tokens-1), TTFT tails and relevant draft, KV, preemption, goodput or replay counters. Confirm small gains with at least five alternating paired full-run blocks, drift checks and intervals; avoid request-level pseudoreplication. Missing telemetry or inadequately covered zero hits is inconclusive. Exclude profiled measurements from the serving frontier.
criteria.justification: The evaluator contract is unusually specific, and likely effects may depend on padding, rank skew, prefix reuse or load. A discriminating experiment deserves substantial weight because it can expose a useful mechanism or cheaply falsify one without an existing bottleneck measurement.

criteria.description: Separate observed results, source-author claims, source fixes and transfer inference. Use short exact quotations and inspect the implementation or engineering artifact supporting the proposed mechanism. Record source hardware, workload, effect size and limitations as unknown whenever absent. Investigate negative results and branch/deployment restrictions. A paper abstract does not establish implementation behavior; prior ranking prose does not establish current source membership.
criteria.justification: No direct evidence accompanies this request. Traceability matters, but demanding multiple publications would unnecessarily exclude straightforward flag changes and small implementation fixes. One relevant engineering source can be sufficient.

criteria.description: Prefer inexpensive falsification, manageable integration and rollback, and benefits exposed by the primary workload. Identify when value is confined to a diagnostic regime. Consider memory pressure, quality, tail latency and throughput tradeoffs. Use parameterized eight-GPU node cost until H200 pricing is known. Across the five selections, favor complementary mechanisms and workload coverage to reduce redundant experiments, without requiring unpublished techniques.
criteria.justification: The requested output is a diverse, practical experiment shortlist. A cheap planner or scheduling change and a larger communication or long-context port can both merit consideration, but their integration costs, activation opportunities and learning value differ.

evidence.rationale: Require one directly relevant engineering source per supported selection, such as implementation code, a patch, a reproducible issue or a dispatch trace; multiple independent sources and papers are not universal requirements. Missing evidence defers qualification rather than proving the idea ineffective. Inspect relevant full-text methods/results if relying on a paper beyond its abstract. Observed results: no independent measurements or implementation artifacts are supplied; available_evidence is empty, and the runtime details are user-supplied attestation. Author claims: the prior ranking says "the three-file patch applies cleanly" and describes H20 performance runs as using "synthetic acceptance"; neither is verified here. Transfer inference: these statements motivate source and activation checks, not H200 gain predictions. The target hardware and workload are specified; candidate-specific hardware, workload, effect sizes and limitations remain unknown except where explicitly attributed to unverified ranking statements. Current dispatch, measured bottlenecks, H200 effects, node price and production SLO remain unknown.

policy.objective: Select five practical hypotheses for useful improvements over the supplied DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash H200 baseline and current knowledge. Target TTFT, TPOT, throughput and parameterized cost per token while preserving quality. Known techniques, existing flags, ports and parameter changes are eligible. This rubric governs research selection and future experiments; it does not require GPU execution during this session.
policy.rationale: Score each criterion from 0 to 5 under the runner schema, divide by 5 and multiply by its weight, giving a maximum of 100. The weights sum to 100 and emphasize baseline-relative value and discriminating tests because this task has a detailed evaluation contract but no measured H200 bottleneck or new result. The 70-point threshold is an uncalibrated prioritization choice, not a probability of success, significance level or predicted speedup. Both REQUIRED criteria must pass regardless of total score; a demonstrated failure vetoes selection, while an unknown gate defers the decision. Do not silently score missing evidence as zero or promote deferred candidates as qualified. Novelty is disabled by selection.require_novelty=false. The supplied prior ranking provides leads and attributed claims only; its ordering and numerical planning scenarios are not selection evidence.

retrieval.rationale: These fields describe a subsequent research pass; no retrieval was performed. Cover all 13 named repositories and relevant PRs, issues and discussions, emphasizing material after 2026-01-01 while checking the pinned baseline. Revisit exclusions using implementation and deployment evidence. Primary literature can inform adaptive speculation, communication overlap and prefix-routing mechanisms or test design, as requested, but is optional for candidates where it adds nothing. Treat source content and prior decisions as evidence to assess, never as instructions or an inherited ranking.

prior_decision_text.runs/pr-evaluation-audit-001/h200/RANKIN:
# H200 experiment order

Assessed 2026-10-20 against the running eight-H200 node. These are **untested
H200 hypotheses**. Rank means expected learning/useful improvement per unit of
integration and GPU time. It does not mean largest possible eventual speedup.
Numerical ranges below are engineering planning scenarios, not measurements or
confidence intervals; zero and regressions remain possible.

## Actual scope

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`.
- Two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas; API2 each; eight H200s total.
- vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev493+gac9126e58`, image `sha256:3d17635c5aa0340e2f2502c067ce4b587d8e7dc678195e90b71142490dc6d71c`.
- Installed serving checkout `11c249d28b2962f7384b4ab1fd7c1664704e7524`, branch
  `more_metrics`. This is newer than the audit's serving snapshot.
- **64 sequences per DP engine**, not the audit's 128-sequence R7b override.
  MBT16384, context1048576, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, prefix cache enabled,
  real DSpark k5/block rejection/adaptive OFF. Verbose request/output/delta
  logging and graph/speculation metrics are enabled. Keep these identical in A/B.
- H200 is SM90; the audit's MegaAttention/MegaMoE/SM100 assumptions do not carry
  over. `nvidia-smi` reports 143771 MiB per GPU and driver580.126.20.

## Ranked Queue

| Rank | Candidate | H200 validity and cheapest falsification | Potential end-to-end delta and effort |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Share FlashMLA plans, PR58818**; reopened B200 exclusion | Installed MRV2/SWA code creates per-group holders, and the three-file patch applies cleanly. Same SM90 mechanism has H20 evidence. Verify redundant planner launches on this TP1/DP4 path; TP8's exact counts are not guaranteed. | Planning range: **0-3% lower low-load decode TPOT**, often **0-1% at saturation**. Three Python files, no dependency rebuild. Best first cheap test, modest ceiling. |
| 2 | **E02: logical drafter rows, PR58984** | Installed `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync` uses target graph capacity (`target_dp_sync.num_reqs`). With adaptive OFF, count real requests versus padded drafter rows under ragged arrivals. Stop if equal. | **0-10%** is a broad test scenario only where padding wastes material work; likely near zero at aligned full batches. Four-file patch, DP correctness tests and an older-base port review. |
| 3 | **E04: CPU DP collectives, PR61767** | New `cpu_all_reduce_` is absent in inspected installed files. Both replicas synchronize four DP ranks. Measure exposed CPU collective time, excluding rank-arrival skew. | **0-5%** scenario if dispatch gaps dominate; zero if hidden by GPU work. More distributed correctness risk than #1. No kernel/toolchain rebuild expected. |
| 4 | **E07: draft token-budget accounting, PR59468** | Check reservations and budget-limited prefill admission at existing MBT16384. Real bound here is **64*(5-1)=256 tokens/rank**, only **1.5625%** of the budget. | Usually near-zero decode gain; potentially small burst TTFT improvement. Budget fraction is **not** a speedup bound or prediction. A lower-MBT experiment would be a different arm. |
| 5 | **E10: host Engram allocation/placement** | Offload and DP sharing/sharding exist, but resolve the actual branch before choosing #59849, #59923 or #62359. Verify NUMA locality and allocator capabilities. | No defensible numeric serving estimate yet. Most plausible in prefill/host-memory stalls. Registration/NUMA branches differ; GB200 cuMem results are not H200 guarantees. |
| 6 | **E11/E14: prefix-group and final-rank locality** | Measure actual prefix misses per rank on agent-f75/sessions. API2 matters; endpoint affinity is already different from DP-rank affinity. | Could improve TTFT substantially on demonstrated misses; **zero expected benefit on the selected cache-isolated first diagnostic**. Do not adopt older-V4 patches unchanged. |
| 7 | **E12/E13: scheduler work and prefill alignment** | Measure host scheduling spans and rank skew under mixed prefill/decode. Revalidate source membership per patch. | Profile-dependent; no justified percentage yet. More likely to affect tails than short homogeneous decode. |
| 8 | **SM90 candidate-only indexer scoring, issue61830** | Real Hopper gap: candidate consumers compute dense logits then mask them. Existing SM100 sparse-MQA route cannot be enabled on H200. Needs an actual Hopper implementation. | Larger long-context ceiling, but poor first-test time-to-value. H20 report puts four consumer layers at **20% of a 1M-context step** at one tested load: even perfect removal implies at most **25% throughput** there before other effects. This says nothing comparable about 1K/8K traffic. |
| 9 | **E15/E18: fusion or alternate Hopper MoE/communication backend** | TP1 may expose useful fusion/communication changes; kernel and precision eligibility must be established first. Current MoE all-to-all config is `allgather_reducescatter`. | Potentially larger gains but integration, numerical and memory risk. Separate backend/precision/topology arms; no percentage justified from the current audit. |

Primary evidence: [#58818](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58818),
[#58984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58984),
[#61767](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61767),
[#59468](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59468),
[SM90 indexer request #61830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61830).
The remaining source links and restrictions are in the original experiment cards.

## Important Rejections

| Audit direction | H200 disposition |
|---|---|
| E01 / #61039 length-aware candidate selection | **Do not cherry-pick as a ready H200 win.** `has_deep_select()` in installed `sparse_mqa_logits.py:43` requires SM100. Upstream's length-aware route uses it; the fallback keeps full-width scoring/top-k. A Hopper port is separate work. |
| E06 / #60802 DeepSelect dispatch | Installed `IndexerTopKDispatcher` also gates DeepSelect to SM100. The proposed route is unavailable on this H200 build. |
| E03 / graph cap512 ->768/1024 and #62040 | **No immediate experiment at seq64.** Live startup captured target FULL(384 tokens,64 requests,q6) and draft FULL(320,64,q5). The specific largest-batch hole is absent. Reopen on runtime fallback or a later seq128 arm, not by copying B200 settings. |
| E05 MegaMoE JIT warmup | Separate startup objective; Blackwell MegaMoE patch is not a steady-state Hopper improvement. Existing startup was already in progress. |
| E08 packed MX activation chain, E09 B200 FlashMLA#227, SM100 routes in E18 | Not eligible as direct Hopper changes. These need architecture-specific ports or a different backend hypothesis. |
| E16 KV tier, E17 draft-context/adaptive changes | Offload tier is inactive; short-context pilot does not trigger long-draft degradation. Added features/output changes have lower first-experiment ROI. |

The source-level H200 exclusions are supported by the installed code and
[#61039's implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7c3f7e5500c85aacb72aab50bd1ce05485b1d73a/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py).
The graph-hole mechanism is documented in
[#62040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62040).

## Why #58818 First

The upstream H20 author reports +2.5% output TPS at C1 and +0.5% at C64, with
synthetic acceptance in the performance runs. We will use real rejection and
the actual H200 TP1/DP4 topology. Those differences limit transferability. The
upstream correctness runs used real verification, but their unit tests did
**not** exercise the newly shared-cache branch. Our candidate is unqualified
until that branch and actual decode behavior are checked.

For intuition, if duplicate plans cost 0.3 ms on a 15 ms critical-path step,
removing them saves 2% step latency and raises ideal throughput by about 2.04%.
The H200 planner count/time and exposed fraction must be measured. Neither
GPU bandwidth ratios nor the PR's microbenchmark multiplier predicts serving
throughput.

Keep a measured no-win outcome: a 0.5% effect below boot/run variation is a
reason to move to #58984, not to keep running until a favorable sample appears.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compare S1 against S0 with identical math, weight representation, and all non-configuration components; record chosen GEMM configurations and kernel timings.
alternatives.explanation: The published bundle benefit may primarily arise from BF16 expansions, mHC changes, Marlin padding, or other components rather than launch configurations.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Audit effective settings and counters, join requests to final DP ranks, and compare prefix-hit tokens, accepted tokens, graph fallbacks, usable KV capacity, and exact output lengths. Treat unmatched factors as separate arms.
alternatives.explanation: A cross-engine gain may come from changed prefix reuse, speculation, memory capacity, graph coverage, or request processing.

card.applicability: Qualification deferred pending parity and shape-dispatch checks. TP8-tuned matrices may differ from TP1 matrices. A runnable engine with unsupported target semantics is an unmatched configuration study, not evidence of improvement over the supplied baseline.
card.code_surface: Source: python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/configs/*NVIDIA_H200*dtype=fp8_w8a8*block_shape=[32, 32]*.json and their GEMM dispatch consumers. Inspect python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py and fp8_utils.py to separate configuration tuning from weight expansion and arithmetic changes. Exact target-shape eligibility and final patch contents are unknown.

evidence.quote: Hopper retains its existing Torch selection path.

experiment.control: A: supplied pinned vLLM baseline, including Marlin selection subject to all-rank verification. S0: pinned SGLang with the same model/tokenizer semantics, two TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas/API2-equivalent frontend capacity, seq64, token/context limits, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram across DP, prefix caching, DSpark k5 probabilistic/block rejection, adaptive OFF, no bounded replay, and equivalent telemetry. Strong static comparator: best existing fixed eligible GEMM configuration selected on a disjoint calibration set.
experiment.correctness: Run applicable G01–G05 once their definitions are available. Check tokenizer/chat/tool/reasoning behavior, stop conditions, prefix reuse, FP8 KV page handling, DSpark rejection and rollback, graph/eager parity, and all-rank collective participation. Verify tuning preserves quantization boundaries and assess numerical/output differences on paired quality tasks with truncations recorded. Aggregate equal scores or nonsignificant differences do not establish equivalence. The reported multi-node startup deadlock warrants targeted checks, not an assumed failure of this independent-EP4 layout.
experiment.cost: Source/configuration parity checking is the inexpensive first gate. A second engine environment and configuration ablation add integration cost of unknown size. Startup and steady-state costs must be reported separately. Use P8*T/(3600*N_out), with node price P8 unset, plus a qualified-output denominator.
experiment.held_out_condition: Reserve distinct agent sessions and Mooncake arrival traces. Evaluate long-context, ragged mixed prefill/decode, and cold/warm prefix conditions separately; retain cache-isolated 1K/1K as a diagnostic. Keep topology changes and seq128 outside this arm.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Parity, final-rank attribution, kernel dispatch, or speculation counters are unverified; other bundle changes cannot be isolated; intervals are too wide; or performance depends on unreported output-length, cache, or memory differences.
experiment.metrics: All-rank tuned-kernel hits divided by eligible group32 GEMM calls, with M/N/K, selected configuration, phase, and graph coverage. Record request TPOT=(last-first token time)/(server output tokens-1), TTFT tails, exact server input/output tokens, node throughput, qualified goodput, replay lag, draft/verify/accepted deltas, prefix-hit tokens by final rank, KV blocks, preemption, peak memory, and errors. Separate profiled GEMM attribution from unprofiled serving results.
experiment.rejects_if: Inspection finds no applicable untuned shapes or no useful configuration delta; matching requirements are demonstrably unsupported without a credible remedy; or adequately precise serving results rule out practical improvement or establish regression. A tuning win that still loses to vLLM is not a deployment win.
experiment.supports_if: S1 activates on relevant shapes, passes correctness, and beats the strongest static S0 configuration by the preregistered useful-gain margin with corresponding exposed GEMM savings. Deployment improvement additionally requires S1 to beat A on a primary workload under matched semantics and quality/latency guardrails.
experiment.treatment: First inspect whether exact deployment semantics, target shapes, and tuning-only controls exist. Establish S0 readiness and correctness before timing. S1 changes only applicable group32 configuration entries. Measure A versus S0 as an engine comparison, S0 versus S1 as the tuning attribution, and A versus S1 for deployment value. Use attestation, activation, correctness, unprofiled native-workload screening, separate mechanism profiling, then at least five alternating paired full-run confirmation blocks for small gains, with drift checks and full-run intervals.

card.mechanism: Transfer inference: fixed GEMM launch configurations better matched to actual Hopper matrix shapes may reduce inefficient tiling or execution overhead without changing operand formats. A matched SGLang control distinguishes this configuration effect from engine-wide scheduling and implementation differences.

novelty.implementation: An explicitly matched SGLang deployment plus configuration-only ablation; no new kernel mechanism claimed.
novelty.scientific: Known kernel configuration tuning and controlled engine comparison.
novelty.specific_delta: Separates engine choice from group32 tuning and removes checkpoint, topology, replay, Engram, and numeric-recipe confounding before claiming baseline-relative value.
novelty.workload: Moves evaluation from cache-flushed random TP8 traffic to native prefixes and fixed arrival schedules under two EP4 replicas.

card.observed_bottleneck: No target GEMM bottleneck is measured. Observed supplied artifact: the baseline startup excerpt selects MARLIN, without all-rank execution proof. Author report: #41251's eight-H200 bundle achieves output-throughput/GPU ratios of 2.0574–2.3498 against its SGLang-main control over three alternating paired sweeps of random 8K/1K traffic. Group32 tuning's isolated effect is unknown. Source topology, checkpoint, Engram, replay, and memory settings differ; source benchmark speculation configuration is unknown.
card.predicted_direction: Conditionally lower GEMM time, decode TPOT, and cost per output token. TTFT or throughput may improve if these GEMMs are exposed. Engine-level direction and effect size remain unknown; tuning may tie or regress on target shapes.
card.proposed_change: First construct a source/configuration parity matrix and inspect shape/config dispatch. If eligible, define S0 as a pinned matched SGLang control and S1 as the same build with only applicable H200 group32 configuration changes. Disable or hold constant every other #41251 component through verified controls or a minimal configuration-only ablation. Do not substitute TP8, device Engram, different activation formats, or different speculation to obtain a runnable matched arm.
card.revision_reason: Unchanged mechanism reconsidered under this task and policy; original decision retained
card.statement: Evaluate a workload-matched SGLang control, then isolate its H200 group32 GEMM configuration tuning as the first optimization arm. The supplied #41251 reports substantial H200 improvements from a multi-change SGLang bundle, but compares against SGLang main under TP8/EP1, another checkpoint, disabled host Engram, and bounded replay. Those results cannot predict an engine replacement here. criteria.description: REQUIRED VETO: Identify a credible, testable mechanism connecting the proposed change to task value, plus either a concrete baseline delta or an explicit cheap source/configuration/log inspection that determines whether the feature is already present and active. criteria.description: Separate observed results, source-author claims, source fixes and transfer inference. criteria.justification: No direct evidence accompanies this request. Traceability matters, but demanding multiple publications would unnecessarily exclude straightforward flag changes and small implementation fixes. One relevant engineering source can be sufficient.

criteria.description: Prefer inexpensive falsification, manageable integration and rollback, and benefits exposed by the primary workload. Identify when value is confined to a diagnostic regime. criteria.justification: The requested output is a diverse, practical experiment shortlist. A cheap planner or scheduling change and a larger communication or long-context port can both merit consideration, but their integration costs, activation opportunities and learning value differ.

evidence.rationale: Require one directly relevant engineering source per supported selection, such as implementation code, a patch, a reproducible issue or a dispatch trace; multiple independent sources and papers are not universal requirements. policy.rationale: Score each criterion from 0 to 5 under the runner schema, divide by 5 and multiply by its weight, giving a maximum of 100. prior_decision_text.runs/pr-evaluation-audit-001/h200/RANKIN:
# H200 experiment order

Assessed 2026-10-20 against the running eight-H200 node. These are **untested
H200 hypotheses**. Rank means expected learning/useful improvement per unit of
integration and GPU time. It does not mean largest possible eventual speedup.
Numerical ranges below are engineering planning scenarios, not measurements or
confidence intervals; zero and regressions remain possible.

## Actual scope

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027`.
- Two independent TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas; API2 each; eight H200s total.
- vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev493+gac9126e58`, image `sha256:3d17635c5aa0340e2f2502c067ce4b587d8e7dc678195e90b71142490dc6d71c`.
- Installed serving checkout `11c249d28b2962f7384b4ab1fd7c1664704e7524`, branch
  `more_metrics`. This is newer than the audit's serving snapshot.
- **64 sequences per DP engine**, not the audit's 128-sequence R7b override.
  MBT16384, context1048576, FP8 KV/block64, host Engram, prefix cache enabled,
  real DSpark k5/block rejection/adaptive OFF. Verbose request/output/delta
  logging and graph/speculation metrics are enabled. Keep these identical in A/B.
- H200 is SM90; the audit's MegaAttention/MegaMoE/SM100 assumptions do not carry
  over. `nvidia-smi` reports 143771 MiB per GPU and driver580.126.20.

## Ranked Queue

| Rank | Candidate | H200 validity and cheapest falsification | Potential end-to-end delta and effort |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Share FlashMLA plans, PR58818**; reopened B200 exclusion | Installed MRV2/SWA code creates per-group holders, and the three-file patch applies cleanly. Same SM90 mechanism has H20 evidence. Verify redundant planner launches on this TP1/DP4 path; TP8's exact counts are not guaranteed. | Planning range: **0-3% lower low-load decode TPOT**, often **0-1% at saturation**. Three Python files, no dependency rebuild. Best first cheap test, modest ceiling. |
| 2 | **E02: logical drafter rows, PR58984** | Installed `_build_uniform_batch_dp_sync` uses target graph capacity (`target_dp_sync.num_reqs`). With adaptive OFF, count real requests versus padded drafter rows under ragged arrivals. Stop if equal. | **0-10%** is a broad test scenario only where padding wastes material work; likely near zero at aligned full batches. Four-file patch, DP correctness tests and an older-base port review. |
| 3 | **E04: CPU DP collectives, PR61767** | New `cpu_all_reduce_` is absent in inspected installed files. Both replicas synchronize four DP ranks. Measure exposed CPU collective time, excluding rank-arrival skew. | **0-5%** scenario if dispatch gaps dominate; zero if hidden by GPU work. More distributed correctness risk than #1. No kernel/toolchain rebuild expected. |
| 4 | **E07: draft token-budget accounting, PR59468** | Check reservations and budget-limited prefill admission at existing MBT16384. Real bound here is **64*(5-1)=256 tokens/rank**, only **1.5625%** of the budget. | Usually near-zero decode gain; potentially small burst TTFT improvement. Budget fraction is **not** a speedup bound or prediction. A lower-MBT experiment would be a different arm. |
| 5 | **E10: host Engram allocation/placement** | Offload and DP sharing/sharding exist, but resolve the actual branch before choosing #59849, #59923 or #62359. Verify NUMA locality and allocator capabilities. | No defensible numeric serving estimate yet. Most plausible in prefill/host-memory stalls. Registration/NUMA branches differ; GB200 cuMem results are not H200 guarantees. |
| 6 | **E11/E14: prefix-group and final-rank locality** | Measure actual prefix misses per rank on agent-f75/sessions. API2 matters; endpoint affinity is already different from DP-rank affinity. | Could improve TTFT substantially on demonstrated misses; **zero expected benefit on the selected cache-isolated first diagnostic**. Do not adopt older-V4 patches unchanged. |
| 7 | **E12/E13: scheduler work and prefill alignment** | Measure host scheduling spans and rank skew under mixed prefill/decode. Revalidate source membership per patch. | Profile-dependent; no justified percentage yet. More likely to affect tails than short homogeneous decode. |
| 8 | **SM90 candidate-only indexer scoring, issue61830** | Real Hopper gap: candidate consumers compute dense logits then mask them. Existing SM100 sparse-MQA route cannot be enabled on H200. Needs an actual Hopper implementation. | Larger long-context ceiling, but poor first-test time-to-value. H20 report puts four consumer layers at **20% of a 1M-context step** at one tested load: even perfect removal implies at most **25% throughput** there before other effects. This says nothing comparable about 1K/8K traffic. |
| 9 | **E15/E18: fusion or alternate Hopper MoE/communication backend** | TP1 may expose useful fusion/communication changes; kernel and precision eligibility must be established first. Current MoE all-to-all config is `allgather_reducescatter`. | Potentially larger gains but integration, numerical and memory risk. Separate backend/precision/topology arms; no percentage justified from the current audit. |

Primary evidence: [#58818](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58818),
[#58984](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58984),
[#61767](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61767),
[#59468](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59468),
[SM90 indexer request #61830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61830).
The remaining source links and restrictions are in the original experiment cards.

## Important Rejections

| Audit direction | H200 disposition |
|---|---|
| E01 / #61039 length-aware candidate selection | **Do not cherry-pick as a ready H200 win.** `has_deep_select()` in installed `sparse_mqa_logits.py:43` requires SM100. Upstream's length-aware route uses it; the fallback keeps full-width scoring/top-k. A Hopper port is separate work. |
| E06 / #60802 DeepSelect dispatch | Installed `IndexerTopKDispatcher` also gates DeepSelect to SM100. The proposed route is unavailable on this H200 build. |
| E03 / graph cap512 ->768/1024 and #62040 | **No immediate experiment at seq64.** Live startup captured target FULL(384 tokens,64 requests,q6) and draft FULL(320,64,q5). The specific largest-batch hole is absent. Reopen on runtime fallback or a later seq128 arm, not by copying B200 settings. |
| E05 MegaMoE JIT warmup | Separate startup objective; Blackwell MegaMoE patch is not a steady-state Hopper improvement. Existing startup was already in progress. |
| E08 packed MX activation chain, E09 B200 FlashMLA#227, SM100 routes in E18 | Not eligible as direct Hopper changes. These need architecture-specific ports or a different backend hypothesis. |
| E16 KV tier, E17 draft-context/adaptive changes | Offload tier is inactive; short-context pilot does not trigger long-draft degradation. Added features/output changes have lower first-experiment ROI. |

The source-level H200 exclusions are supported by the installed code and
[#61039's implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7c3f7e5500c85aacb72aab50bd1ce05485b1d73a/vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py).
The graph-hole mechanism is documented in
[#62040](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62040).

## Why #58818 First

The upstream H20 author reports +2.5% output TPS at C1 and +0.5% at C64, with
synthetic acceptance in the performance runs. We will use real rejection and
the actual H200 TP1/DP4 topology. Those differences limit transferability. The
upstream correctness runs used real verification, but their unit tests did
**not** exercise the newly shared-cache branch. Our candidate is unqualified
until that branch and actual decode behavior are checked.

For intuition, if duplicate plans cost 0.3 ms on a 15 ms critical-path step,
removing them saves 2% step latency and raises ideal throughput by about 2.04%.
The H200 planner count/time and exposed fraction must be measured. Neither
GPU bandwidth ratios nor the PR's microbenchmark multiplier predicts serving
throughput.

Keep a measured no-win outcome: a 0.5% effect below boot/run variation is a
reason to move to #58984, not to keep running until a favorable sample appears.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compare current allocation, exact-size cudaHostAlloc and exact-size registered storage under identical sorting, page policy and NUMA placement.
alternatives.explanation: Exact sizing saves memory but registration type, not byte reduction, causes lookup improvement.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Inspect ownership and physical backing before porting; then measure exposed lookup time rather than standalone kernel duration. Reject this delta if the relevant allocation branch is absent.
alternatives.explanation: The live tables are already shared/exact-sized, or lookup work is hidden by overlap.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compare supported existing configurations. Record their sorting and page-policy differences explicitly rather than attributing all changes to registration.
alternatives.explanation: Existing THP or NUMA placement delivers the practical benefit more simply.

card.applicability: CUDA-host allocation path is plausibly portable to H200, but registration capability and effective allocation mode are unknown. Shared or already exact-sized tables may have no delta. Required gates remain deferred until source and backing inspection.
card.code_surface: vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py; tests/kernels/test_engram.py; distributed Engram tests. The supplied PR describes the helper change and tests but does not supply its implementation diff.

evidence.quote: Exact size gives the memory saving; the registered memory type gives the speed.
Decode lookups already overlap on the side stream.

experiment.control: Attested allocation with matched NUMA placement and sorting. Include exact-size cudaHostAlloc as an attribution control and the strongest supported existing THP/placement configuration as a practical comparator.
experiment.correctness: Check exact table bytes and lookup outputs at shard and allocation boundaries, sorted/unsorted paths, empty and uneven batches, registration fallback, teardown and repeated allocation/free. Exercise graph replay and distributed storage lifetime. If outputs or math change unexpectedly, require numerical and quality qualification rather than acceptance statistics. Map relevant cases to G01-G05 once supplied.
experiment.cost: Cheap allocation inspection, then moderate allocator/lifetime validation. Host-memory savings are not GPU KV savings or an automatic node-price reduction. Use C8*T/(3600*Nqualified), with C8 unknown.
experiment.held_out_condition: Primary native agent-f75 and Mooncake at seq64. Hold out cold/warm allocation phases, long and ragged prefills, repeated versus random row IDs, and simultaneous memory pressure from both replicas. Keep random-row microbenchmarks separate.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Storage ownership, physical-memory accounting or registration telemetry is unresolved, host pressure is unrepresentative, or serving differences remain within drift.
experiment.metrics: Denominator: private offloaded table allocations eligible for exact registration; numerator: successful exact registrations, with fallback counts. Track logical bytes, actual registered bytes, physical host usage without double-counting shared mappings, faults, pressure and NUMA traffic. Measure lookup rows and exposed lookup time, TTFT tails, request TPOT, exact tokens, qualified goodput, KV/preemption, draft counters and replay lag on all ranks.
experiment.rejects_if: Tables are already exact/shared with no relevant delta; registration is unsupported; lookup gains remain entirely hidden; no serving value appears under adequately covered relevant conditions; or lifetime/correctness failures occur. Record memory-only savings separately.
experiment.supports_if: The eligible branch activates and reduces actual allocation waste; serving qualification additionally requires lower exposed stalls or lookup time and better unprofiled metrics than the strongest comparator. Confirm small effects with at least five alternating paired full-run blocks and held-out checks.
experiment.treatment: First inspect effective allocation and source presence. If eligible, change only exact-size registration and fallback handling; qualify before unprofiled serving tests.

card.mechanism: Source fix: reuse the registration helper without huge pages for exact-sized private offloaded tables, falling back on registration failure. Transfer inference: less allocation waste may relieve real host pressure, while a different backing/registration path may independently alter exposed lookup latency.

novelty.implementation: Port an existing private-table allocator change only after resolving the actual storage branch.
novelty.nearest_prior_art: vLLM PR #59849. PR #62359 addresses a different shared-storage branch; PR #59923 addresses packed sharded exchange.
novelty.scientific: Known exact-allocation and registration techniques; no novelty claim.
novelty.specific_delta: Remove demonstrated private allocation rounding and change its registration path without changing ownership, precision or exchange.
novelty.workload: Separate host-memory accounting from serving impact on real prefixes and speculation-expanded row counts.

card.observed_bottleneck: Unknown on H200. Author-reported GB10 TP4, 32K-token measurements reduced host allocation from 33.1 to 24.3 GiB with registration. Exact cudaHostAlloc used 24.9 GiB but retained the same 41.4 ms unsorted lookup time; registered storage reported 22.7 ms. End-to-end offload validation was still outstanding. These sizes and timings do not establish TP1/DP4 behavior.
card.predicted_direction: Lower physical host allocation if rounding exists; potentially lower TTFT or higher throughput only with demonstrable pressure or exposed lookup savings. Decode benefit and all H200 effect sizes are unknown.
card.proposed_change: Inspect effective defaults, storage ownership, allocator calls, physical/shared bytes and NUMA placement across both replicas. Only for an eligible rounded private-table path, adapt #59849. Keep table values, sorting thresholds, partitioning and communication unchanged; do not bundle packed exchange or shared cuMem backing.
card.revision_reason: Unchanged mechanism reconsidered under this task and policy; original decision retained
card.statement: Test exact-size registration of CPU-offloaded Engram tables only after resolving whether this deployment uses private DP shards or shared host storage. The launch arguments establish offload and embedding_across_dp, but do not establish allocation ownership, rounding or backing. PR #59849 separates two effects: exact sizing reduces host allocation, while registration type changes lookup performance in its GB10 experiment. If the live private-table path still rounds allocations, port that allocation change with safe fallback and unchanged sorting and NUMA placement. Compare against exact-size cudaHostAlloc and supported existing THP settings. Predict serving benefit only if host pressure or exposed lookup latency falls; memory savings alone do not establish lower H200 cost per token.

criteria.description: Specify the activation signal and eligible-opportunity denominator, competing explanations, strongest simple comparator, scoped correctness checks, held-out test and prospective support/reject/inconclusive rules. criteria.description: Separate observed results, source-author claims, source fixes and transfer inference. Use short exact quotations and inspect the implementation or engineering artifact supporting the proposed mechanism. A paper abstract does not establish implementation behavior; prior ranking prose does not establish current source membership.
criteria.justification: No direct evidence accompanies this request. Traceability matters, but demanding multiple publications would unnecessarily exclude straightforward flag changes and small implementation fixes. One relevant engineering source can be sufficient.

criteria.description: Prefer inexpensive falsification, manageable integration and rollback, and benefits exposed by the primary workload. Identify when value is confined to a diagnostic regime. Across the five selections, favor complementary mechanisms and workload coverage to reduce redundant experiments, without requiring unpublished techniques.
criteria.justification: The requested output is a diverse, practical experiment shortlist. A cheap planner or scheduling change and a larger communication or long-context port can both merit consideration, but their integration costs, activation opportunities and learning value differ.

evidence.rationale: Require one directly relevant engineering source per supported selection, such as implementation code, a patch, a reproducible issue or a dispatch trace; multiple independent sources and papers are not universal requirements. Missing evidence defers qualification rather than proving the idea ineffective. Inspect relevant full-text methods/results if relying on a paper beyond its abstract. Observed results: no independent measurements or implementation artifacts are supplied; available_evidence is empty, and the runtime details are user-supplied attestation. Author claims: the prior ranking says "the three-file patch applies cleanly" and describes H20 performance runs as using "synthetic acceptance"; neither is verified here. Transfer inference: these statements motivate source and activation checks, not H200 gain predictions. The target hardware and workload are specified; candidate-specific hardware, workload, effect sizes and limitations remain unknown except where explicitly attributed to unverified ranking statements. Current dispatch, measured bottlenecks, H200 effects, node price and production SLO remain unknown.

policy.objective: Select five practical hypotheses for useful improvements over the supplied DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash H200 baseline and current knowledge. This rubric governs research selection and future experiments; it does not require GPU execution during this session.
policy.rationale: Score each criterion from 0 to 5 under the runner schema, divide by 5 and multiply by its weight, giving a maximum of 100. The weights sum to 100 and emphasize baseline-relative value and discriminating tests because this task has a detailed evaluation contract but no measured H200 bottleneck or new result. The 70-point threshold is an uncalibrated prioritization choice, not a probability of success, significance level or predicted speedup. Both REQUIRED criteria must pass regardless of total score; a demonstrated failure vetoes selection, while an unknown gate defers the decision. Do not silently score missing evidence as zero or promote deferred candidates as qualified. Novelty is disabled by selection.require_novelty=false. The supplied prior ranking provides leads and attributed claims only; its ordering and numerical planning scenarios are not selection evidence.

Cover all 13 named repositories and relevant PRs, issues and discussions, emphasizing material after 2026-01-01 while checking the pinned baseline.
